explanatories.mul_inv_rev: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the product of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the product of their individual inverses in reverse order.

MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.code:
MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer'.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Group α] [MulAction α β]
  {φ : Quotient (orbitRel α β) → β} (hφ : LeftInverse Quotient.mk'' φ) :
  β ≃ (ω : Quotient (orbitRel α β)) × α ⧸ stabilizer α (φ ω)
MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.comment:
**Class formula** : given `G` a group acting on `X` and `φ` a function mapping each orbit of `X`
under this action (that is, each element of the quotient of `X` by the relation `orbitRel G X`) to
an element in this orbit, this gives a (noncomputable) bijection between `X` and the disjoint union
of `G/Stab(φ(ω))` over all orbits `ω`. In most cases you'll want `φ` to be `Quotient.out'`, so we
provide `MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer'` as a special case.

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.
explanatories.MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient.orbit: This definition describes the set of elements in the orbit associated with a specific element of the quotient formed by the orbits of a group action.
explanatories.MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbits': This definition describes a bijective correspondence between an element and its orbits under a group action, representing the structure of the entire type as a disjoint union of these orbits.
explanatories.Equiv.sigmaCongrRight: This definition indicates that a collection of equivalent types leads to an overall equivalence between the dependent sum of those types.
explanatories.Equiv.Set.ofEq: The definition states that if two sets are equal, then there exists an equivalence relation between their elements.
explanatories.MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient.orbit_eq_orb: This theorem indicates that for an element in the quotient of an orbit under group action, the orbit of that element is equivalent to the orbit formed by applying the group actions to a representative element obtained through a right inverse function.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.trans: The composition of two embeddings results in a new embedding that maps elements from the first type to the third type through the intermediate type.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.fullDefinition: noncomputable def selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer' {φ : Ω → β}     (hφ : LeftInverse Quotient.mk'' φ) : β ≃ Σω : Ω, α ⧸ stabilizer α (φ ω) :=   calc     β ≃ Σω : Ω, orbitRel.Quotient.orbit ω := selfEquivSigmaOrbits' α β     _ ≃ Σω : Ω, α ⧸ stabilizer α (φ ω) :=       Equiv.sigmaCongrRight fun ω =>         (Equiv.Set.ofEq <| orbitRel.Quotient.orbit_eq_orbit_out _ hφ).trans <|           orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer α (φ ω)
MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.description: This definition establishes a bijection between a set acted upon by a group and a disjoint union of quotient spaces formed by the stabilizers of elements within each orbit of that action.

mul_action.self_equiv_sigma_orbits_quoti.code:
MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer'.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Group α] [MulAction α β]
  {φ : Quotient (orbitRel α β) → β} (hφ : LeftInverse Quotient.mk'' φ) :
  β ≃ (ω : Quotient (orbitRel α β)) × α ⧸ stabilizer α (φ ω)
mul_action.self_equiv_sigma_orbits_quoti.comment:
**Class formula** : given `G` a group acting on `X` and `φ` a function mapping each orbit of `X`
under this action (that is, each element of the quotient of `X` by the relation `orbitRel G X`) to
an element in this orbit, this gives a (noncomputable) bijection between `X` and the disjoint union
of `G/Stab(φ(ω))` over all orbits `ω`. In most cases you'll want `φ` to be `Quotient.out'`, so we
provide `MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer'` as a special case.

MulAction.card_eq_sum_card_group_div_car.code:
MulAction.card_eq_sum_card_group_div_card_stabilizer'.{u, v} (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [Group α] [MulAction α β]
  [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype (Quotient (orbitRel α β))] [(b : β) → Fintype ↥(stabilizer α b)]
  {φ : Quotient (orbitRel α β) → β} (hφ : LeftInverse Quotient.mk'' φ) :
  Fintype.card β = ∑ ω : Quotient (orbitRel α β), Fintype.card α / Fintype.card ↥(stabilizer α (φ ω))
MulAction.card_eq_sum_card_group_div_car.comment:
**Class formula** for a finite group acting on a finite type. See
`MulAction.card_eq_sum_card_group_div_card_stabilizer` for a specialized version using
`Quotient.out'`.

explanatories.Quotient.mk'': This definition outlines a way to create an equivalence class from an element by using a setoid as an implicit argument rather than as a specified instance.
explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.Quotient: The quotient of a set using an equivalence relation is a type that represents the distinct equivalence classes formed by that relation.
explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.
explanatories.Nat.card: This definition assigns a natural number representing the cardinality of a type, with the convention that infinite types are assigned the value zero.

MulAction.card_eq_sum_card_group_div_car.description: This theorem expresses that the total number of elements in a set that a finite group acts on is equal to the sum of the sizes of the orbits divided by the sizes of their stabilizers, illustrating the class formula for finite group actions.

MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.comment:
**Class formula**. This is a special case of
`MulAction.self_equiv_sigma_orbits_quotient_stabilizer'` with `φ = Quotient.out'`.

explanatories.Quotient.out': This defines a function that retrieves an element from a quotient type by using an explicit setoid as a parameter.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.out_eq': This theorem asserts that the image of an element in the quotient group, when projected back to the group, equals the original equivalence class represented by that element.
explanatories.MulAction.stabilizer: This definition characterizes the stabilizer of an element under a group action as the subgroup of elements that leave that specific element unchanged.
explanatories.AddAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt: This definition establishes a bijection between a set acted upon by a group and a disjoint union of quotient spaces formed by the stabilizers of elements within each orbit of that action.
explanatories.MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt: This definition establishes a bijection between a set acted upon by a group and a disjoint union of quotient spaces formed by the stabilizers of elements within each orbit of that action.
explanatories.Quotient.out_eq': The theorem establishes that for any quotient of a setoid, the operation of reconstructing the original quotient from its representative yields the same quotient.

MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.fullDefinition: noncomputable def selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer : β ≃ Σω : Ω, α ⧸ stabilizer α ω.out' :=   selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientStabilizer' α β Quotient.out_eq'
MulAction.selfEquivSigmaOrbitsQuotientSt.description: This definition establishes a bijection between a set acted upon by a group and a disjoint union of quotient spaces formed by the stabilizer of each represented orbit of that action, specifically using the natural projection from the quotient.

Equiv.Perm.swapFactorsAux.fullDefinition: def swapFactorsAux :     ∀ (l : List α) (f : Perm α),       (∀ {x}, f x ≠ x → x ∈ l) → { l : List (Perm α) // l.prod = f ∧ ∀ g ∈ l, IsSwap g }   | [] => fun f h =>     ⟨[],       Equiv.ext fun x => by         rw [List.prod_nil]         exact (Classical.not_not.1 (mt h (List.not_mem_nil _))).symm,       by simp⟩   | x::l => fun f h =>     if hfx : x = f x then       swapFactorsAux l f fun {y} hy =>         List.mem_of_ne_of_mem (fun h : y = x => by simp [h, hfx.symm] at hy) (h hy)     else       let m :=         swapFactorsAux l (swap x (f x) * f) fun {y} hy =>           have : f y ≠ y ∧ y ≠ x := ne_and_ne_of_swap_mul_apply_ne_self hy           List.mem_of_ne_of_mem this.2 (h this.1)       ⟨swap x (f x)::m.1, by         rw [List.prod_cons, m.2.1, ← mul_assoc, mul_def (swap x (f x)), swap_swap, ← one_def,           one_mul],         fun {g} hg => ((List.mem_cons).1 hg).elim (fun h => ⟨x, f x, hfx, h⟩) (m.2.2 _)⟩

  G ≃* ↥(MulAction.toPermHom G H).range
Equiv.Perm.subgroupOfMulAction.comment:
**Cayley's theorem**: Every group G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group acting on
`G`. Note that we generalize this to an arbitrary "faithful" group action by `G`. Setting `H = G`
recovers the usual statement of Cayley's theorem via `RightCancelMonoid.faithfulSMul`

explanatories.MonoidHom.range: The range of a monoid homomorphism from one group to another forms a subgroup of the target group.
explanatories.MulAction.toPermHom: This definition establishes a correspondence between elements of a group and permutations of a set, where each group element induces a specific permutation on the set.
explanatories.MulEquiv.ofLeftInverse': A monoid homomorphism with a left-inverse establishes a multiplicative equivalence between its domain and its range.
explanatories.Classical.choose_spec: Selecting an element that satisfies a property guarantees that this element indeed possesses that property.
explanatories.MulAction.toPerm_injective: This theorem establishes that the mapping from group elements to permutations induced by a faithful action of a group on a set is injective, meaning distinct group elements yield distinct permutations.
explanatories.Function.Injective.hasLeftInverse: There is no theorem or definition provided, so no mathematical or logical concept can be summarized.

equiv.perm.is_cycle.zpowers_equiv_suppor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def IsCycle.zpowersEquivSupport {σ : Perm α} (hσ : IsCycle σ) :     (Subgroup.zpowers σ) ≃ σ.support :=   Equiv.ofBijective     (fun (τ : ↥ ((Subgroup.zpowers σ) : Set (Perm α))) =>       ⟨(τ : Perm α) (Classical.choose hσ), by         obtain ⟨τ, n, rfl⟩ := τ         erw [Finset.mem_coe, Subtype.coe_mk, zpow_apply_mem_support, mem_support]         exact (Classical.choose_spec hσ).1⟩)     (by       constructor       · rintro ⟨a, m, rfl⟩ ⟨b, n, rfl⟩ h         ext y         by_cases hy : σ y = y         · simp_rw [zpow_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_self hy]         · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := (Classical.choose_spec hσ).2 hy           rw [Subtype.coe_mk, Subtype.coe_mk, zpow_apply_comm σ m i, zpow_apply_comm σ n i]           exact congr_arg _ (Subtype.ext_iff.mp h)       · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩         erw [Finset.mem_coe, mem_support] at hy         obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := (Classical.choose_spec hσ).2 hy         exact ⟨⟨σ ^ n, n, rfl⟩, rfl⟩)

Equiv.Perm.cycleFactorsAux.fullDefinition: def cycleFactorsAux [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] :     ∀ (l : List α) (f : Perm α),       (∀ {x}, f x ≠ x → x ∈ l) →         { l : List (Perm α) // l.prod = f ∧ (∀ g ∈ l, IsCycle g) ∧ l.Pairwise Disjoint } := by   intro l f h   exact match l with   | [] => ⟨[], by       { simp only [imp_false, List.Pairwise.nil, List.not_mem_nil, forall_const, and_true_iff,           forall_prop_of_false, Classical.not_not, not_false_iff, List.prod_nil] at *         ext         simp [*]}⟩   | x::l =>     if hx : f x = x then cycleFactorsAux l f (by         intro y hy; exact List.mem_of_ne_of_mem (fun h => hy (by rwa [h])) (h hy))     else       let ⟨m, hm₁, hm₂, hm₃⟩ :=         cycleFactorsAux l ((cycleOf f x)⁻¹ * f) (by         intro y hy         exact List.mem_of_ne_of_mem             (fun h : y = x => by               rw [h, mul_apply, Ne, inv_eq_iff_eq, cycleOf_apply_self] at hy               exact hy rfl)             (h fun h : f y = y => by               rw [mul_apply, h, Ne, inv_eq_iff_eq, cycleOf_apply] at hy               split_ifs at hy <;> tauto))       ⟨cycleOf f x::m, by         rw [List.prod_cons, hm₁]         simp,         fun g hg ↦ ((List.mem_cons).1 hg).elim (fun hg => hg.symm ▸ isCycle_cycleOf _ hx) (hm₂ g),         List.pairwise_cons.2           ⟨fun g hg y =>             or_iff_not_imp_left.2 fun hfy =>               have hxy : SameCycle f x y :=                 Classical.not_not.1 (mt cycleOf_apply_of_not_sameCycle hfy)               have hgm : (g::m.erase g) ~ m :=                 List.cons_perm_iff_perm_erase.2 ⟨hg, List.Perm.refl _⟩               have : ∀ h ∈ m.erase g, Disjoint g h :=                 (List.pairwise_cons.1 ((hgm.pairwise_iff Disjoint.symm).2 hm₃)).1               by_cases id fun hgy : g y ≠ y =>                 (disjoint_prod_right _ this y).resolve_right <| by                   have hsc : SameCycle f⁻¹ x (f y) := by                     rwa [sameCycle_inv, sameCycle_apply_right]                   rw [disjoint_prod_perm hm₃ hgm.symm, List.prod_cons,                       ← eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq] at hm₁                   rwa [hm₁, mul_apply, mul_apply, cycleOf_inv, hsc.cycleOf_apply, inv_apply_self,                     inv_eq_iff_eq, eq_comm],             hm₃⟩⟩

equiv.perm.cycle_factors_aux.comment:
Given a list `l : List α` and a permutation `f : Perm α` whose nonfixed points are all in `l`,
recursively factors `f` into cycles.

explanatories.Equiv.Perm.SameCycle: This definition establishes an equivalence relation that determines whether two elements belong to the same cycle within a given permutation.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.sameCycle_apply_right: This theorem asserts that an element remains in the same cycle under a permutation regardless of whether it is compared to another element or its image under the permutation.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.cycleOf_apply: Applying a permutation to an element results in the permutation's effect on that element if they belong to the same cycle, otherwise it remains unchanged.
explanatories.Equiv.ext: This theorem asserts that if two equivalences agree on their mappings for all elements, then they are identical equivalences.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.inv_eq_iff_eq: This theorem relates the equality of an element resulting from applying the inverse of a permutation to another element with the equivalence of the original element being mapped by the permutation to that second element.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.sameCycle_inv: This theorem states that two elements are in the same cycle of a permutation if and only if they are also in the same cycle when considering the inverse of that permutation.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.cycleOf_inv: The inverse of the cycle of a permutation that includes a specific element is equivalent to the cycle of that element in the inverse permutation.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.mul_apply: This theorem states that the application of the product of two permutations to an element is equivalent to applying the second permutation followed by the first permutation to that element.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.SameCycle.cycleOf_apply: If two elements belong to the same cycle of a permutation, then applying the cycle to one of the elements results in the same outcome as applying the permutation to that element directly.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.cycleOf_apply_of_not_sameCycl: If two elements do not belong to the same cycle of a permutation, then applying the cycle to one of the elements leaves it unchanged.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.SameCycle.symm: This theorem states that if two elements are in the same cycle of a permutation, then they are also in the same cycle when their positions are swapped.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.mt: If a true implication leads to a false conclusion, then the antecedent must also be false.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.SameCycle.rfl: This theorem states that an element is in the same cycle as itself for any given permutation.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.cycleOf_apply_self: Applying a permutation to an element within its cycle results in the same outcome as directly applying the permutation to that element.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.IsCycle: This definition describes a cycle in a permutation as a non-identity arrangement where any two elements that are not fixed can be connected through repeated applications of the permutation.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Classical.not_not: The Double Negation Theorem states that the negation of the negation of a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.SameCycle.refl: This theorem asserts that any element is in the same cycle as itself within a given permutation.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.cycleOf: The cycle of a permutation for a specific element is either the identity if the element is fixed or the permutation itself if the element is not fixed.
explanatories.False.elim: From a contradiction, any proposition can be inferred, illustrating that if something is false, anything follows.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.isCycle_cycleOf: The cycle of a permutation that includes an element, which does not remain unchanged by the permutation, is indeed a cycle.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.Disjoint: Two permutations are considered disjoint if they fix different elements, meaning no element is affected by both permutations simultaneously.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.Disjoint.symm: If two permutations are disjoint, then the first permutation is also disjoint from the second.
explanatories.not_false_iff: The statement establishes that the negation of falsehood is logically equivalent to truth.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.List.prod: This definition describes the operation that computes the product of all elements in a list, starting with the identity element of multiplication.
explanatories.List.nil: The empty list is represented by the notation for an empty collection with no elements.
explanatories.imp_false: A proposition implying a contradiction is equivalent to the negation of that proposition.
explanatories.List.not_mem_nil: This theorem states that no element can be a member of an empty list.
explanatories.forall_const: For any nonempty type, a constant function to a proposition is equivalent to that proposition itself.
explanatories.and_true_iff: Theorem stating that a conjunction of a proposition with a truth value is equivalent to the original proposition itself.
explanatories.forall_prop_of_false: If a proposition is false, then the universal quantification over another proposition derived from it is equivalent to asserting that the latter is always true.
explanatories.List.prod_nil: The product of an empty list is defined to be the identity element of multiplication.
explanatories.List.mem_of_ne_of_mem: This theorem shows that if an element is not equal to the head of a non-empty list and is a member of that list, then it must also be a member of the tail of the list.
explanatories.Classical.or_iff_not_imp_left: The statement asserts that the disjunction of two propositions is equivalent to the implication that if the first is false, then the second must be true.
explanatories.List.prod_cons: This theorem states that the product of a list with a head element is equal to the product of the head element and the product of the remainder of the list.
explanatories.List.mem_cons: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of a non-empty list if and only if it is equal to the head of the list or a member of the tail of the list.
explanatories.Or.elim: This theorem establishes that if at least one of two propositions is true and both imply a third proposition, then the third proposition must also be true.
explanatories.List.erase: This definition describes a function that removes the first occurrence of a specified element from a list, if it exists.
explanatories.by_cases: This theorem asserts that if a proposition can lead to another proposition through both its affirmation and negation, then the latter proposition is necessarily true.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.disjoint_prod_right: A permutation that is disjoint from each element in a list of permutations is also disjoint from the product of those permutations.
explanatories.Or.resolve_right: This theorem states that if at least one of two propositions is true and the second proposition is false, then the first proposition must be true.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.disjoint_prod_perm: The product of two lists of disjoint permutations is equal if one list is a permutation of the other.
explanatories.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq: The equation relating an element to the product of the inverse of another element and a third element is equivalent to the product of the second element and the first element being equal to that third element in a group.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.inv_apply_self: This theorem asserts that applying the inverse of a permutation to an element that has already been permuted by that permutation returns the original element.
explanatories.eq_comm: The equality relation between two elements is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.ext: This theorem asserts that if two permutations are identical on all elements of a set, then the permutations themselves are equal.
explanatories.Set.Pairwise: A relation holds pairwise on a set if it is true for every distinct pair of elements within that set.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.
explanatories.symm: This theorem establishes that if a binary relation is symmetric, then holding the relation between two elements implies that it also holds in the reverse order between those elements.

explanatories.Multiset.sum_replicate: The sum of the elements in a multiset created by replicating a single element a certain number of times equals the product of that number and the element itself.

explanatories.IsConj.trans: This theorem demonstrates that if one element in a monoid is conjugate to a second element, and that second element is conjugate to a third element, then the first element is also conjugate to the third element.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Nat.ModEq.trans: This theorem demonstrates that if one natural number is congruent to a second under a specific modulus, and that second number is congruent to a third under the same modulus, then the first number is also congruent to the third.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.VectorsProdEqOne.card: The number of vectors of a specified length that multiply to one in a group is equal to the number of group elements raised to the power of one less than that length.
explanatories.add_tsub_cancel_of_le: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another in an ordered structure, then adding the difference between these two elements to the smaller element results in the larger element.
explanatories.Multiset.mem_add: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of the sum of two multisets if and only if it is a member of at least one of the individual multisets.
explanatories.zero_lt_one: Zero is strictly less than one in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.lt_of_lt_of_le: This theorem shows that if one element is less than a second element, and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than the third element in a preorder.
explanatories.ge_of_eq: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is greater than or equal to the other.
explanatories.Multiset.eq_of_mem_replicate: This theorem states that if an element appears in a multiset created by repeating another element a certain number of times, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.Nat.Partition.parts: The parts of a partition of a natural number consist of the positive integers that add up to that number.

Equiv.Perm.partition.fullDefinition: def partition (σ : Perm α) : (Fintype.card α).Partition where   parts := σ.cycleType + Multiset.replicate (Fintype.card α - σ.support.card) 1   parts_pos {n hn} := by     cases' mem_add.mp hn with hn hn     · exact zero_lt_one.trans (one_lt_of_mem_cycleType hn)     · exact lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one (ge_of_eq (Multiset.eq_of_mem_replicate hn))   parts_sum := by     rw [sum_add, sum_cycleType, Multiset.sum_replicate, nsmul_eq_mul, Nat.cast_id, mul_one,       add_tsub_cancel_of_le σ.support.card_le_univ]
Equiv.Perm.partition.description: The partition corresponding to a permutation describes how the elements of a set are divided into disjoint subsets based on the action of the permutation.

Equiv.Perm.toCycle.fullDefinition: def toCycle (f : Perm α) (hf : IsCycle f) : Cycle α :=   Multiset.recOn (Finset.univ : Finset α).val (Quot.mk _ [])     (fun x _ l => if f x = x then l else toList f x)     (by       intro x y _ s       refine heq_of_eq ?_       split_ifs with hx hy hy <;> try rfl       have hc : SameCycle f x y := IsCycle.sameCycle hf hx hy       exact Quotient.sound' hc.toList_isRotated)

Equiv.Perm.isoCycle.fullDefinition: def isoCycle : { f : Perm α // IsCycle f } ≃ { s : Cycle α // s.Nodup ∧ s.Nontrivial } where   toFun f := ⟨toCycle (f : Perm α) f.prop, nodup_toCycle f f.prop, nontrivial_toCycle _ f.prop⟩   invFun s := ⟨(s : Cycle α).formPerm s.prop.left, (s : Cycle α).isCycle_formPerm _ s.prop.right⟩   left_inv f := by     obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := id f.prop     simpa [toCycle_eq_toList (f : Perm α) f.prop x hx, formPerm_toList, Subtype.ext_iff] using       f.prop.cycleOf_eq hx   right_inv s := by     rcases s with ⟨⟨s⟩, hn, ht⟩     obtain ⟨x, -, -, hx, -⟩ := id ht     have hl : 2 ≤ s.length := by simpa using Cycle.length_nontrivial ht     simp only [Cycle.mk_eq_coe, Cycle.nodup_coe_iff, Cycle.mem_coe_iff, Subtype.coe_mk,       Cycle.formPerm_coe] at hn hx ⊢     apply Subtype.ext     dsimp     rw [toCycle_eq_toList _ _ x]     · refine Quotient.sound' ?_       exact toList_formPerm_isRotated_self _ hl hn _ hx     · rw [← mem_support, support_formPerm_of_nodup _ hn]       · simpa using hx       · rintro _ rfl         simp [Nat.succ_le_succ_iff] at hl

Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin.comment:
Permutations of `Fin (n + 1)` are equivalent to fixing a single
`Fin (n + 1)` and permuting the remaining with a `Perm (Fin n)`.
The fixed `Fin (n + 1)` is swapped with `0`.

unitsCenterToCenterUnits.comment:

unitsCenterToCenterUnits.fullDefinition: def unitsCenterToCenterUnits [Monoid M] : (Submonoid.center M)ˣ →* Submonoid.center (Mˣ) :=   (Units.map (Submonoid.center M).subtype).codRestrict _ <|       fun u ↦ Submonoid.mem_center_iff.mpr <|         fun r ↦ Units.ext <| by         rw [Units.val_mul, Units.coe_map, Submonoid.coe_subtype, Units.val_mul, Units.coe_map,           Submonoid.coe_subtype, u.1.prop.comm r]
unitsCenterToCenterUnits.description: The units of the center of a monoid can be associated with the center of the units of that monoid through a homomorphism.

explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.Submonoid.coe_mul: The product of two elements from a submonoid is equal to the product of their images in the larger monoid.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.Submonoid.leftInv: The leftInverse submonoid of a given submonoid consists of all elements that serve as left inverses within that submonoid.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.Submonoid.fromLeftInv: This defines a function that maps elements from the left inverse submonoid of a submonoid to their corresponding right inverses in the original submonoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.mul_fromLeftInv: For any element in the left inverse submonoid of a submonoid, multiplying it by its corresponding right inverse yields the identity element.
explanatories.Submonoid.fromLeftInv_one: The mapping of the identity element from the left inverse submonoid of a submonoid to its corresponding right inverse in the original submonoid is itself the identity element.
explanatories.Submonoid.fromLeftInv_eq_iff: The value produced by the function mapping from the left inverse submonoid to the original submonoid is equal to a given element if and only if the product of the left inverse and that element equals one.
explanatories.OneHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a one homomorphism between two types that each have a one element.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_mul': This theorem states that a certain function maintains the operation of multiplication across the elements it acts upon.
explanatories.Submonoid.ext: Two submonoids are considered identical if every element in one is also an element of the other.

Submonoid.fromCommLeftInv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def fromCommLeftInv : S.leftInv →* S where   toFun := S.fromLeftInv   map_one' := S.fromLeftInv_one   map_mul' x y :=     Subtype.ext <| by       rw [fromLeftInv_eq_iff, mul_comm x, Submonoid.coe_mul, Submonoid.coe_mul, mul_assoc, ←         mul_assoc (x : M), mul_fromLeftInv, one_mul, mul_fromLeftInv]
Submonoid.fromCommLeftInv.description: The mapping from the left inverse submonoid of a commutative submonoid to the submonoid itself assigns each element to its right inverse within that submonoid.

explanatories.Units.inv_val: The product of the inverse value and the value of a unit element in a monoid equals one.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.
explanatories.Exists.choose_spec: An element chosen from an existence assertion satisfies the property asserted by that existence statement.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Subtype.eq: If two elements of a subtype have the same underlying value, then they are considered equal as elements of that subtype.

Submonoid.leftInvEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def leftInvEquiv : S.leftInv ≃* S :=   { S.fromCommLeftInv with     invFun := fun x ↦ by       choose x' hx using hS x.prop       exact ⟨x'.inv, x, hx ▸ x'.inv_val⟩     left_inv := fun x ↦       Subtype.eq <| by         dsimp only; generalize_proofs h; rw [← h.choose.mul_left_inj]         conv => rhs; rw [h.choose_spec]         exact h.choose.inv_val.trans (S.mul_fromLeftInv x).symm     right_inv := fun x ↦ by       dsimp only [fromCommLeftInv]       ext       rw [fromLeftInv_eq_iff]       convert (hS x.prop).choose.inv_val       exact (hS x.prop).choose_spec.symm }
Submonoid.leftInvEquiv.description: The left inverse submonoid of a submonoid consisting entirely of units is structurally isomorphic to the original submonoid through a multiplicative equivalence.

AddSubmonoid.leftNegEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def leftInvEquiv : S.leftInv ≃* S :=   { S.fromCommLeftInv with     invFun := fun x ↦ by       choose x' hx using hS x.prop       exact ⟨x'.inv, x, hx ▸ x'.inv_val⟩     left_inv := fun x ↦       Subtype.eq <| by         dsimp only; generalize_proofs h; rw [← h.choose.mul_left_inj]         conv => rhs; rw [h.choose_spec]         exact h.choose.inv_val.trans (S.mul_fromLeftInv x).symm     right_inv := fun x ↦ by       dsimp only [fromCommLeftInv]       ext       rw [fromLeftInv_eq_iff]       convert (hS x.prop).choose.inv_val       exact (hS x.prop).choose_spec.symm }

Con.mapOfSurjective.fullDefinition: def mapOfSurjective (f : M → N) (H : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y) (h : mulKer f H ≤ c)     (hf : Surjective f) : Con N :=   { c.toSetoid.mapOfSurjective f h hf with     mul' := fun h₁ h₂ => by       rcases h₁ with ⟨a, b, rfl, rfl, h1⟩       rcases h₂ with ⟨p, q, rfl, rfl, h2⟩       exact ⟨a * p, b * q, by rw [H], by rw [H], c.mul h1 h2⟩ }

Con.comap.{u_1, u_2} {M : Type u_1} {N : Type u_2} [Mul M] [Mul N] (f : M → N) (H : ∀ (x y : M), f (x * y) = f x * f y)
  (c : Con N) : Con M
Con.comap.comment:
Given types with multiplications `M, N` and a congruence relation `c` on `N`, a
multiplication-preserving map `f : M → N` induces a congruence relation on `f`'s domain
defined by '`x ≈ y` iff `f(x)` is related to `f(y)` by `c`.'

Con.comap.fullDefinition: def comap (f : M → N) (H : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y) (c : Con N) : Con M :=   { c.toSetoid.comap f with     mul' := @fun w x y z h1 h2 => show c (f (w * y)) (f (x * z)) by rw [H, H]; exact c.mul h1 h2 }
Con.comap.description: This definition describes how a multiplication-preserving map induces a congruence relation on its domain based on the equivalence relation defined in the codomain.

Con.correspondence.fullDefinition: def correspondence : { d // c ≤ d } ≃o Con c.Quotient where   toFun d :=     d.1.mapOfSurjective (↑) _ (by rw [mul_ker_mk_eq]; exact d.2) <|       @Quotient.exists_rep _ c.toSetoid   invFun d :=     ⟨comap ((↑) : M → c.Quotient) (fun x y => rfl) d, fun x y h =>       show d x y by rw [c.eq.2 h]; exact d.refl _⟩   left_inv d :=     -- Porting note: by exact needed for unknown reason     by exact       Subtype.ext_iff_val.2 <|         ext fun x y =>           ⟨fun h =>             let ⟨a, b, hx, hy, H⟩ := h             d.1.trans (d.1.symm <| d.2 <| c.eq.1 hx) <| d.1.trans H <| d.2 <| c.eq.1 hy,             fun h => ⟨_, _, rfl, rfl, h⟩⟩   right_inv d :=     -- Porting note: by exact needed for unknown reason     by exact       ext fun x y =>         ⟨fun h =>           let ⟨_, _, hx, hy, H⟩ := h           hx ▸ hy ▸ H,           Con.induction_on₂ x y fun w z h => ⟨w, z, rfl, rfl, h⟩⟩   map_rel_iff' := @fun s t => by     constructor     · intros h x y hs       rcases h ⟨x, y, rfl, rfl, hs⟩ with ⟨a, b, hx, hy, ht⟩       exact t.1.trans (t.1.symm <| t.2 <| Quotient.eq_rel.1 hx)         (t.1.trans ht (t.2 <| Quotient.eq_rel.1 hy))     · intros h _ _ hs       rcases hs with ⟨a, b, hx, hy, Hs⟩       exact ⟨a, b, hx, hy, h Hs⟩
Con.correspondence.description: This definition establishes an order-preserving bijection between congruence relations that contain a given multiplicative congruence on a type and the congruence relations defined on the quotient of that type by the given congruence.

Con.quotientKerEquivRange.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotientKerEquivRange (f : M →* P) : (ker f).Quotient ≃* MonoidHom.mrange f :=   { Equiv.ofBijective         ((@MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MonoidHom.mrange (kerLift f)) _ _ _ <|               MulEquiv.submonoidCongr kerLift_range_eq).comp           (kerLift f).mrangeRestrict) <|       ((Equiv.bijective (@MulEquiv.toEquiv (MonoidHom.mrange (kerLift f)) _ _ _ <|           MulEquiv.submonoidCongr kerLift_range_eq)).comp         ⟨fun x y h =>           kerLift_injective f <| by rcases x with ⟨⟩; rcases y with ⟨⟩; injections,           fun ⟨w, z, hz⟩ => ⟨z, by rcases hz with ⟨⟩; rfl⟩⟩) with     map_mul' := MonoidHom.map_mul _ }
Con.quotientKerEquivRange.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the quotient of the kernel of a monoid homomorphism and the submonoid corresponding to the image of that homomorphism, reflecting the first isomorphism theorem for monoids.

Con.quotientKerEquivOfRightInverse.fullDefinition: def quotientKerEquivOfRightInverse (f : M →* P) (g : P → M) (hf : Function.RightInverse g f) :     (ker f).Quotient ≃* P :=   { kerLift f with     toFun := kerLift f     invFun := (↑) ∘ g     left_inv := fun x => kerLift_injective _ (by rw [Function.comp_apply, kerLift_mk, hf])     right_inv := fun x => by (conv_rhs => rw [← hf x]); rfl }

Con.map_of_mul_left_rel_one.code:
Con.map_of_mul_left_rel_one.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} [Monoid M] (c : Con M) (f : M → M) (hf : ∀ (x : M), c (f x * x) 1)
  {x y : M} (h : c x y) : c (f x) (f y)
Con.map_of_mul_left_rel_one.comment:
Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter.

Subgroup.Saturated.comment:

FreeGroup.Red.decidableRel.fullDefinition: instance Red.decidableRel : DecidableRel (@Red α)   | [], [] => isTrue Red.refl   | [], _hd2 :: _tl2 => isFalse fun H => List.noConfusion (Red.nil_iff.1 H)   | (x, b) :: tl, [] =>     match Red.decidableRel tl [(x, not b)] with     | isTrue H => isTrue <| Red.trans (Red.cons_cons H) <| (@Red.Step.not _ [] [] _ _).to_red     | isFalse H => isFalse fun H2 => H <| Red.cons_nil_iff_singleton.1 H2   | (x1, b1) :: tl1, (x2, b2) :: tl2 =>     if h : (x1, b1) = (x2, b2) then       match Red.decidableRel tl1 tl2 with       | isTrue H => isTrue <| h ▸ Red.cons_cons H       | isFalse H => isFalse fun H2 => H <| (Red.cons_cons_iff _).1 <| h.symm ▸ H2     else       match Red.decidableRel tl1 ((x1, ! b1) :: (x2, b2) :: tl2) with       | isTrue H => isTrue <| (Red.cons_cons H).tail Red.Step.cons_not       | isFalse H => isFalse fun H2 => H <| Red.inv_of_red_of_ne h H2

IsFreeGroupoid.actionGroupoidIsFree.comment:
An action groupoid over a free group is free. More generally, one could show that the groupoid
of elements over a free groupoid is free, but this version is easier to prove and suffices for our
purposes.

Analogous to the fact that a covering space of a graph is a graph. (A free groupoid is like a graph,
and a groupoid of elements is like a covering space.)

is_free_groupoid.action_groupoid_is_free.fullDefinition: instance actionGroupoidIsFree {G A : Type u} [Group G] [IsFreeGroup G] [MulAction G A] :     IsFreeGroupoid (ActionCategory G A) where   quiverGenerators :=     ⟨fun a b => { e : IsFreeGroup.Generators G // IsFreeGroup.of e • a.back = b.back }⟩   of := fun (e : { e // _}) => ⟨IsFreeGroup.of e, e.property⟩   unique_lift := by     intro X _ f     let f' : IsFreeGroup.Generators G → (A → X) ⋊[mulAutArrow] G := fun e =>       ⟨fun b => @f ⟨(), _⟩ ⟨(), b⟩ ⟨e, smul_inv_smul _ b⟩, IsFreeGroup.of e⟩     rcases IsFreeGroup.unique_lift f' with ⟨F', hF', uF'⟩     refine ⟨uncurry F' ?_, ?_, ?_⟩     · suffices SemidirectProduct.rightHom.comp F' = MonoidHom.id _ by         -- Porting note: `MonoidHom.ext_iff` has been deprecated.         exact DFunLike.ext_iff.mp this       apply IsFreeGroup.ext_hom (fun x ↦ ?_)       rw [MonoidHom.comp_apply, hF']       rfl     · rintro ⟨⟨⟩, a : A⟩ ⟨⟨⟩, b⟩ ⟨e, h : IsFreeGroup.of e • a = b⟩       change (F' (IsFreeGroup.of _)).left _ = _       rw [hF']       cases inv_smul_eq_iff.mpr h.symm       rfl     · intro E hE       have : curry E = F' := by         apply uF'         intro e         ext         · convert hE _ _ _           rfl         · rfl       apply Functor.hext       · intro         apply Unit.ext       · refine ActionCategory.cases ?_         intros         simp only [← this, uncurry_map, curry_apply_left, coe_back, homOfPair.val]         rfl

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End: This definition describes the collection of endomorphisms of an object in a category, where the order of multiplication corresponds to function composition rather than the composition defined in category theory.
explanatories.IsFreeGroupoid.SpanningTree.loopOfHom: This definition states that any morphism in a groupoid can be transformed into a loop at a given root of a spanning tree by applying conjugation with homomorphisms derived from the tree structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.End.one_def: This theorem establishes that the multiplicative identity in the context of endomorphisms of an object in a category is equal to the identity morphism of that object.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_one: This theorem states that a monoid homomorphism preserves the identity element, asserting that the image of the identity in the source is the identity in the target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.SingleObj.id_as_one: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism in a single-object category is equivalent to the identity element of the associated monoid.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.SingleObj.comp_as_mul: This theorem establishes that the composition of morphisms in a single-object category corresponds to multiplication in the associated monoid.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_mul: If a function is a monoid homomorphism, it preserves the operation by ensuring that the result of applying the function to the product of two elements is equal to the product of the images of those elements.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.End.mul_def: This theorem establishes that the multiplication of two endomorphisms of an object in a category is equivalent to composing the second endomorphism with the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id: A functor preserves identity morphisms by ensuring that the image of an identity morphism in one category is the identity morphism of the corresponding object in the mapped category.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.

IsFreeGroupoid.SpanningTree.functorOfMon.fullDefinition: def functorOfMonoidHom {X} [Monoid X] (f : End (root' T) →* X) :     G ⥤ CategoryTheory.SingleObj X where   obj _ := ()   map p := f (loopOfHom T p)   map_id := by     intro a     dsimp only [loopOfHom]     rw [Category.id_comp, IsIso.hom_inv_id, ← End.one_def, f.map_one, id_as_one]   map_comp := by     intros     rw [comp_as_mul, ← f.map_mul]     simp only [IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc, loopOfHom, End.mul_def, Category.assoc]
IsFreeGroupoid.SpanningTree.functorOfMon.description: This definition describes a functor that extends a homomorphism defined at the root of a spanning tree in a free groupoid to the entire groupoid, reflecting the structure of the monoid associated with the homomorphism.

AddSubgroup.exists_isLeast_pos.comment:
If a nontrivial additive subgroup of a linear ordered additive commutative group is disjoint
with the interval `Set.Ioo 0 a` for some positive `a`, then the set of positive elements of this

Localization.r.code: Localization.r.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} [CommMonoid M] (S : Submonoid M) : Con (M × ↥S)
Localization.r.comment:
The congruence relation on `M × S`, `M` a `CommMonoid` and `S` a submonoid of `M`, whose
quotient is the localization of `M` at `S`, defined as the unique congruence relation on
`M × S` such that for any other congruence relation `s` on `M × S` where for all `y ∈ S`,
`(1, 1) ∼ (y, y)` under `s`, we have that `(x₁, y₁) ∼ (x₂, y₂)` by `r` implies
`(x₁, y₁) ∼ (x₂, y₂)` by `s`.

Localization.r'.fullDefinition: def r' : Con (M × S) := by   -- note we multiply by `c` on the left so that we can later generalize to `•`   refine     { r := fun a b : M × S ↦ ∃ c : S, ↑c * (↑b.2 * a.1) = c * (a.2 * b.1)       iseqv := ⟨fun a ↦ ⟨1, rfl⟩, fun ⟨c, hc⟩ ↦ ⟨c, hc.symm⟩, ?_⟩       mul' := ?_ }   · rintro a b c ⟨t₁, ht₁⟩ ⟨t₂, ht₂⟩     use t₂ * t₁ * b.2     simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul]     calc       (t₂ * t₁ * b.2 : M) * (c.2 * a.1) = t₂ * c.2 * (t₁ * (b.2 * a.1)) := by ac_rfl       _ = t₁ * a.2 * (t₂ * (c.2 * b.1)) := by rw [ht₁]; ac_rfl       _ = t₂ * t₁ * b.2 * (a.2 * c.1) := by rw [ht₂]; ac_rfl   · rintro a b c d ⟨t₁, ht₁⟩ ⟨t₂, ht₂⟩     use t₂ * t₁     calc       (t₂ * t₁ : M) * (b.2 * d.2 * (a.1 * c.1)) = t₂ * (d.2 * c.1) * (t₁ * (b.2 * a.1)) := by ac_rfl       _ = (t₂ * t₁ : M) * (a.2 * c.2 * (b.1 * d.1)) := by rw [ht₁, ht₂]; ac_rfl

  ∀ (toMonoidHom_1 : M →* N) (map_units'_1 : ∀ (y : ↥S), IsUnit ((↑toMonoidHom_1).toFun ↑y))
    (surj'_1 : ∀ (z : N), ∃ x, z * (↑toMonoidHom_1).toFun ↑x.2 = (↑toMonoidHom_1).toFun x.1)
    (exists_of_eq_1 : ∀ (x y : M), (↑toMonoidHom_1).toFun x = (↑toMonoidHom_1).toFun y → ∃ c, ↑c * x = ↑c * y),
    ({ toMonoidHom := toMonoidHom, map_units' := map_units', surj' := surj', exists_of_eq := exists_of_eq } =
        { toMonoidHom := toMonoidHom_1, map_units' := map_units'_1, surj' := surj'_1,
          exists_of_eq := exists_of_eq_1 }) =
      (toMonoidHom = toMonoidHom_1)

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.sec.comment:

`(x, y) : M × S` such that `f x * (f y)⁻¹ = z`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mul_inv_left.description: This theorem shows that for a given monoid homomorphism from a commutative monoid to another, and for any element of a submonoid, the product of an element with the inverse of the image under the homomorphism is equivalent to a conditional relation involving that element and another element of the codomain.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mk'_sec.{u_1, u_2} {M : Type u_1} [CommMonoid M] {S : Submonoid M} {N : Type u_2}
  [CommMonoid N] (f : S.LocalizationMap N) (z : N) : f.mk' (f.sec z).1 (f.sec z).2 = z
AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.mk'_sec.comment:
Given a localization map `f : M →* N` for a submonoid `S ⊆ M`, for all `z : N` we have that if
`x : M, y ∈ S` are such that `z * f y = f x`, then `f x * (f y)⁻¹ = z`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.exists_of_sec_.comment:
Given a Localization map `f : M →* N` for a Submonoid `S ⊆ M`, for all `x₁ : M` and `y₁ ∈ S`,
if `x₂ : M, y₂ ∈ S` are such that `f x₁ * (f y₁)⁻¹ * f y₂ = f x₂`, then there exists `c ∈ S`
such that `x₁ * y₂ * c = x₂ * y₁ * c`.

`g : M →* P` such that `g y` is invertible for all `y : S`, the homomorphism induced from

`z = f x * (f y)⁻¹`.

explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.OreLocalization.one: The element representing one in the Ore localization is defined as the fraction of one over one.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.map_mul: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.sec: This definition describes a section function that associates an element from the original monoid with a specific element from the localized monoid, ensuring that the localization map applied to the first element multiplied by the inverse of the second equals the given element in the localized structure.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.sec: This definition describes a section function that associates an element from the original monoid with a specific element from the localized monoid, ensuring that the localization map applied to the first element multiplied by the inverse of the second equals the given element in the localized structure.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.sec_spec: This theorem shows that for any element in the target commutative monoid, multiplying it by the image of a specific section from the localization map yields an element in the original monoid that corresponds to that section.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.sec_spec: This theorem shows that for any element in the target commutative monoid, multiplying it by the image of a specific section from the localization map yields an element in the original monoid that corresponds to that section.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.sec_spec': This theorem demonstrates that the image of an element under a localization map equals the product of the image of another associated element and the element itself in the target commutative monoid.
explanatories.IsUnit.liftRight: A homomorphism from one monoid to another can be extended to a homomorphism from the first monoid to the group of units of the second monoid if it maps elements to units.
explanatories.MonoidHom.restrict: The restriction of a monoid homomorphism to a submonoid produces a new homomorphism from the elements of that submonoid to another monoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mul_inv_left: This theorem shows that for a given monoid homomorphism from a commutative monoid to another, and for any element of a submonoid, the product of an element with the inverse of the image under the homomorphism is equivalent to a conditional relation involving that element and another element of the codomain.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mul_inv_right: This theorem states that for a homomorphism from a commutative monoid to another, where the images of elements from a submonoid are units, the equality of two elements is equivalent to the equality involving the inverse of the image of an element from the submonoid.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_mul: If a function is a monoid homomorphism, it preserves the operation by ensuring that the result of applying the function to the product of two elements is equal to the product of the images of those elements.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.eq_of_eq: This theorem establishes that if two elements in a commutative monoid have the same image under a localization map, then they also produce the same result when passed through another monoid homomorphism, provided that the latter homomorphism maps the submonoid's elements to units in the target monoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.eq_of_eq: This theorem establishes that if two elements in a commutative monoid have the same image under a localization map, then they also produce the same result when passed through another monoid homomorphism, provided that the latter homomorphism maps the submonoid's elements to units in the target monoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.sec_spec': This theorem demonstrates that the image of an element under a localization map equals the product of the image of another associated element and the element itself in the target commutative monoid.
explanatories.MulEquiv.map_mul: A multiplicative isomorphism maintains the property of multiplication when mapping elements between two multiplicative structures.
explanatories.OneHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a one homomorphism between two types that each have a one element.
explanatories.OneHom.map_one': This theorem states that a one homomorphism preserves the identity element by mapping it to itself between two types that each have a one element.
explanatories.MonoidHom.map_mul': This theorem states that a certain function maintains the operation of multiplication across the elements it acts upon.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift.fullDefinition: noncomputable def lift : N →* P where   toFun z := g (f.sec z).1 * (IsUnit.liftRight (g.restrict S) hg (f.sec z).2)⁻¹   map_one' := by rw [mul_inv_left, mul_one]; exact f.eq_of_eq hg (by rw [← sec_spec, one_mul])   map_mul' x y := by     dsimp only     rw [mul_inv_left hg, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_right hg, mul_comm _ (g (f.sec y).1), ←       mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_right hg]     repeat rw [← g.map_mul]     exact f.eq_of_eq hg (by simp_rw [f.toMap.map_mul, sec_spec']; ac_rfl)
Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift.description: This definition establishes a method to induce a homomorphism from a localized structure to another commutative monoid, contingent on having an invertible image for every element from the submonoid.

submonoid.localization_map.lift.comment:
Given a Localization map `f : M →* N` for a Submonoid `S ⊆ M` and a map of `CommMonoid`s
`g : M →* P` such that `g y` is invertible for all `y : S`, the homomorphism induced from
`N` to `P` sending `z : N` to `g x * (g y)⁻¹`, where `(x, y) : M × S` are such that
`z = f x * (f y)⁻¹`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift_spec.comment:
Given a Localization map `f : M →* N` for a Submonoid `S ⊆ M`, if a `CommMonoid` map
`g : M →* P` induces a map `f.lift hg : N →* P` then for all `z : N, v : P`, we have
`f.lift hg z = v ↔ g x = g y * v`, where `x : M, y ∈ S` are such that `z * f y = f x`.

AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.lift_add_le.comment:
Given a Localization map `f : M →* N` for a Submonoid `S ⊆ M`, if a `CommMonoid` map
`g : M →* P` induces a map `f.lift hg : N →* P` then for all `z : N`, we have
`g y * f.lift hg z = g x`, where `x : M, y ∈ S` are such that `z * f y = f x`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.map.comment:
Given a `CommMonoid` homomorphism `g : M →* P` where for Submonoids `S ⊆ M, T ⊆ P` we have
`g(S) ⊆ T`, the induced Monoid homomorphism from the Localization of `M` at `S` to the
Localization of `P` at `T`: if `f : M →* N` and `k : P →* Q` are Localization maps for `S` and
`T` respectively, we send `z : N` to `k (g x) * (k (g y))⁻¹`, where `(x, y) : M × S` are such
that `z = f x * (f y)⁻¹`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.map_spec.comment:
Given Localization maps `f : M →* N, k : P →* Q` for Submonoids `S, T` respectively, if a
`CommMonoid` homomorphism `g : M →* P` induces a `f.map hy k : N →* Q`, then for all `z : N`,
`u : Q`, we have `f.map hy k z = u ↔ k (g x) = k (g y) * u` where `x : M, y ∈ S` are such that
`z * f y = f x`.

submonoid.localization_map.map_mul_left.comment:
Given Localization maps `f : M →* N, k : P →* Q` for Submonoids `S, T` respectively, if a
`CommMonoid` homomorphism `g : M →* P` induces a `f.map hy k : N →* Q`, then for all `z : N`,
we have `k (g y) * f.map hy k z = k (g x)` where `x : M, y ∈ S` are such that
`z * f y = f x`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.surj₂.code:
Submonoid.LocalizationMap.surj₂.{u_1, u_2} {M : Type u_1} [CommMonoid M] {S : Submonoid M} {N : Type u_2} [CommMonoid N]
  (f : S.LocalizationMap N) (z w : N) : ∃ z' w' d, z * f.toMap ↑d = f.toMap z' ∧ w * f.toMap ↑d = f.toMap w'
Submonoid.LocalizationMap.surj₂.comment:
Given a localization map `f : M →* N`, and `z w : N`, there exist `z' w' : M` and `d : S`
such that `f z' / f d = z` and `f w' / f d = w`.

Submonoid.LocalizationMap.ofMulEquivOfDo.fullDefinition: def ofMulEquivOfDom {k : P ≃* M} (H : T.map k.toMonoidHom = S) : LocalizationMap T N :=   let H' : S.comap k.toMonoidHom = T :=     H ▸ (SetLike.coe_injective <| T.1.1.preimage_image_eq k.toEquiv.injective)   (f.toMap.comp k.toMonoidHom).toLocalizationMap     (fun y ↦       let ⟨z, hz⟩ := f.map_units ⟨k y, H ▸ Set.mem_image_of_mem k y.2⟩       ⟨z, hz⟩)     (fun z ↦       let ⟨x, hx⟩ := f.surj z       let ⟨v, hv⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective x.1       let ⟨w, hw⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective x.2       ⟨(v, ⟨w, H' ▸ show k w ∈ S from hw.symm ▸ x.2.2⟩),         show z * f.toMap (k.toEquiv w) = f.toMap (k.toEquiv v) by erw [hv, hw, hx]⟩)     fun x y ↦     show f.toMap _ = f.toMap _ → _ by       erw [f.eq_iff_exists]       exact         fun ⟨c, hc⟩ ↦           let ⟨d, hd⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective c           ⟨⟨d, H' ▸ show k d ∈ S from hd.symm ▸ c.2⟩, by             erw [← hd, ← k.map_mul, ← k.map_mul] at hc; exact k.toEquiv.injective hc⟩
Submonoid.LocalizationMap.ofMulEquivOfDo.description: This definition describes a way to create a localization map for one submonoid by composing an existing localization map with an isomorphism that relates two commutative monoids and ensures that the images of the submonoids under this isomorphism are equal.

AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.ofAddEquivO.fullDefinition: def ofMulEquivOfDom {k : P ≃* M} (H : T.map k.toMonoidHom = S) : LocalizationMap T N :=   let H' : S.comap k.toMonoidHom = T :=     H ▸ (SetLike.coe_injective <| T.1.1.preimage_image_eq k.toEquiv.injective)   (f.toMap.comp k.toMonoidHom).toLocalizationMap     (fun y ↦       let ⟨z, hz⟩ := f.map_units ⟨k y, H ▸ Set.mem_image_of_mem k y.2⟩       ⟨z, hz⟩)     (fun z ↦       let ⟨x, hx⟩ := f.surj z       let ⟨v, hv⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective x.1       let ⟨w, hw⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective x.2       ⟨(v, ⟨w, H' ▸ show k w ∈ S from hw.symm ▸ x.2.2⟩),         show z * f.toMap (k.toEquiv w) = f.toMap (k.toEquiv v) by erw [hv, hw, hx]⟩)     fun x y ↦     show f.toMap _ = f.toMap _ → _ by       erw [f.eq_iff_exists]       exact         fun ⟨c, hc⟩ ↦           let ⟨d, hd⟩ := k.toEquiv.surjective c           ⟨⟨d, H' ▸ show k d ∈ S from hd.symm ▸ c.2⟩, by             erw [← hd, ← k.map_mul, ← k.map_mul] at hc; exact k.toEquiv.injective hc⟩

Localization.monoidOf.fullDefinition: def monoidOf : Submonoid.LocalizationMap S (Localization S) :=   { (r S).mk'.comp <| MonoidHom.inl M         S with     toFun := fun x ↦ mk x 1     map_one' := mk_one     map_mul' := fun x y ↦ by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_one]     map_units' := fun y ↦       isUnit_iff_exists_inv.2 ⟨mk 1 y, by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_one, one_mul, mk_self]⟩     surj' := fun z ↦ induction_on z fun x ↦       ⟨x, by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_comm x.fst, ← mk_mul, mk_self, one_mul]⟩     exists_of_eq := fun x y ↦ Iff.mp <|       mk_eq_mk_iff.trans <|         r_iff_exists.trans <|           show (∃ c : S, ↑c * (1 * x) = c * (1 * y)) ↔ _ by rw [one_mul, one_mul] }

localization.monoid_of.fullDefinition: def monoidOf : Submonoid.LocalizationMap S (Localization S) :=   { (r S).mk'.comp <| MonoidHom.inl M         S with     toFun := fun x ↦ mk x 1     map_one' := mk_one     map_mul' := fun x y ↦ by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_one]     map_units' := fun y ↦       isUnit_iff_exists_inv.2 ⟨mk 1 y, by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_one, one_mul, mk_self]⟩     surj' := fun z ↦ induction_on z fun x ↦       ⟨x, by dsimp only; rw [mk_mul, mul_comm x.fst, ← mk_mul, mk_self, one_mul]⟩     exists_of_eq := fun x y ↦ Iff.mp <|       mk_eq_mk_iff.trans <|         r_iff_exists.trans <|           show (∃ c : S, ↑c * (1 * x) = c * (1 * y)) ↔ _ by rw [one_mul, one_mul] }
localization.monoid_of.description: This definition establishes a natural homomorphism that maps elements from a commutative monoid to their corresponding equivalence classes in the localization of that monoid at a specified submonoid.

Monoid.CoprodI.lift.fullDefinition: def lift : (∀ i, M i →* N) ≃ (CoprodI M →* N) where   toFun fi :=     Con.lift _ (FreeMonoid.lift fun p : Σi, M i => fi p.fst p.snd) <|       Con.conGen_le <| by         simp_rw [Con.ker_rel]         rintro _ _ (i | ⟨x, y⟩)         · change FreeMonoid.lift _ (FreeMonoid.of _) = FreeMonoid.lift _ 1           simp only [MonoidHom.map_one, FreeMonoid.lift_eval_of]         · change             FreeMonoid.lift _ (FreeMonoid.of _ * FreeMonoid.of _) =               FreeMonoid.lift _ (FreeMonoid.of _)           simp only [MonoidHom.map_mul, FreeMonoid.lift_eval_of]   invFun f i := f.comp of   left_inv := by     intro fi     ext i x     -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644     erw [MonoidHom.comp_apply, of_apply, Con.lift_mk', FreeMonoid.lift_eval_of]   right_inv := by     intro f     ext i x     rfl

Monoid.CoprodI.Word.consRecOn.fullDefinition: def consRecOn {motive : Word M → Sort*} (w : Word M) (h_empty : motive empty)     (h_cons : ∀ (i) (m : M i) (w) h1 h2, motive w → motive (cons m w h1 h2)) :     motive w := by   rcases w with ⟨w, h1, h2⟩   induction w with   | nil => exact h_empty   | cons m w ih =>     refine h_cons m.1 m.2 ⟨w, fun _ hl => h1 _ (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl), h2.tail⟩ ?_ ?_ (ih _ _)     · rw [List.chain'_cons'] at h2       simp only [fstIdx, ne_eq, Option.map_eq_some',         Sigma.exists, exists_and_right, exists_eq_right, not_exists]       intro m' hm'       exact h2.1 _ hm' rfl     · exact h1 _ (List.mem_cons_self _ _)

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def equivPairAux (i) (w : Word M) : { p : Pair M i // rcons p = w } :=   consRecOn w ⟨⟨1, .empty, by simp [fstIdx, empty]⟩, by simp [rcons]⟩ <|     fun j m w h1 h2 _ =>       if ij : i = j then         { val :=           { head := ij ▸ m             tail := w             fstIdx_ne := ij ▸ h1 }           property := by subst ij; simp [rcons, h2] }       else ⟨⟨1, cons m w h1 h2, by simp [cons, fstIdx, Ne.symm ij]⟩,  by simp [rcons]⟩

  [Group G] {H : ι → Type u_5} [(i : ι) → Group (H i)] (f : (i : ι) → H i →* G) (hcard : 3 ≤ #ι ∨ ∃ i, 3 ≤ #(H i))

  (hXdisj : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (X i) (X j))
  (hpp : Pairwise fun i j => ∀ (h : H i), h ≠ 1 → (f i) h • X j ⊆ X i) : Function.Injective ⇑(lift f)
Monoid.CoprodI.lift_injective_of_ping_po.comment:
The **Ping-Pong-Lemma**.

Given a group action of `G` on `X` so that the `H i` acts in a specific way on disjoint subsets
`X i` we can prove that `lift f` is injective, and thus the image of `lift f` is isomorphic to the
free product of the `H i`.

Often the Ping-Pong-Lemma is stated with regard to subgroups `H i` that generate the whole group;
we generalize to arbitrary group homomorphisms `f i : H i →* G` and do not require the group to be
generated by the images.

Usually the Ping-Pong-Lemma requires that one group `H i` has at least three elements. This
condition is only needed if `# ι = 2`, and we accept `3 ≤ # ι` as an alternative.

FreeGroup.injective_lift_of_ping_pong.code:
FreeGroup.injective_lift_of_ping_pong.{u_1, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} [Nontrivial ι] {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (a : ι → G)
  {α : Type u_4} [MulAction G α] (X Y : ι → Set α) (hXnonempty : ∀ (i : ι), (X i).Nonempty)
  (hXdisj : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (X i) (X j)) (hYdisj : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (Y i) (Y j))
  (hXYdisj : ∀ (i j : ι), Disjoint (X i) (Y j)) (hX : ∀ (i : ι), a i • (Y i)ᶜ ⊆ X i)
  (hY : ∀ (i : ι), a⁻¹ i • (X i)ᶜ ⊆ Y i) : Function.Injective ⇑(FreeGroup.lift a)
FreeGroup.injective_lift_of_ping_pong.comment:
The Ping-Pong-Lemma.

Given a group action of `G` on `X` so that the generators of the free groups act in specific
ways on disjoint subsets `X i` and `Y i` we can prove that `lift f` is injective, and thus the image
of `lift f` is isomorphic to the free group.

Often the Ping-Pong-Lemma is stated with regard to group elements that generate the whole group;
we generalize to arbitrary group homomorphisms from the free group to `G` and do not require the
group to be generated by the elements.

explanatories.Con.lift: This definition describes a homomorphism on the quotient of a monoid, which is induced by a given homomorphism that remains constant across the equivalence classes defined by a particular congruence relation.
explanatories.FreeMonoid.lift: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between functions that map elements to a monoid and monoid homomorphisms from a free monoid generated by those elements to the monoid.
explanatories.Monoid.CoprodI.lift: This definition establishes an equivalence between a family of homomorphisms from individual summands of a free product and a single homomorphism from that free product itself, reflecting the universal property of the free product in category theory.
explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Monoid.CoprodI.Word.empty: This definition refers to the notion of an empty reduced word within a structure of indexed monoids, representing the trivial element of that particular free monoid.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Pairwise: A relation is considered "pairwise" if it holds between every pair of distinct elements in its domain.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.
explanatories.FreeGroup.lift: This definition states that any function from a set to a group uniquely extends to a homomorphism from the free group generated by that set to the group.
explanatories.FreeGroupBasis.lift: This definition describes a natural bijection between functions from a basis of a free group to another group and group homomorphisms from the free group to that group.

FreeGroup.injective_lift_of_ping_pong.description: This theorem demonstrates that a homomorphism from a free group to a group is injective under specific conditions involving disjoint subsets acted on by the group, thereby generalizing the Ping-Pong lemma.

Subgroup.quotientEquivProdOfLE'.fullDefinition: def quotientEquivProdOfLE' (h_le : s ≤ t) (f : α ⧸ t → α)     (hf : Function.RightInverse f QuotientGroup.mk) : α ⧸ s ≃ (α ⧸ t) × t ⧸ s.subgroupOf t where   toFun a :=     ⟨a.map' id fun b c h => leftRel_apply.mpr (h_le (leftRel_apply.mp h)),       a.map' (fun g : α => ⟨(f (Quotient.mk'' g))⁻¹ * g, leftRel_apply.mp (Quotient.exact' (hf g))⟩)         fun b c h => by         rw [leftRel_apply]         change ((f b)⁻¹ * b)⁻¹ * ((f c)⁻¹ * c) ∈ s         have key : f b = f c :=           congr_arg f (Quotient.sound' (leftRel_apply.mpr (h_le (leftRel_apply.mp h))))         rwa [key, mul_inv_rev, inv_inv, mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel_left, ← leftRel_apply]⟩   invFun a := by     refine a.2.map' (fun (b : { x // x ∈ t}) => f a.1 * b) fun b c h => by       rw [leftRel_apply] at h ⊢       change (f a.1 * b)⁻¹ * (f a.1 * c) ∈ s       rwa [mul_inv_rev, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel_left]   left_inv := by     refine Quotient.ind' fun a => ?_     simp_rw [Quotient.map'_mk'', id, mul_inv_cancel_left]   right_inv := by     refine Prod.rec ?_     refine Quotient.ind' fun a => ?_     refine Quotient.ind' fun b => ?_     have key : Quotient.mk'' (f (Quotient.mk'' a) * b) = Quotient.mk'' a :=       (QuotientGroup.mk_mul_of_mem (f a) b.2).trans (hf a)     simp_rw [Quotient.map'_mk'', id, key, inv_mul_cancel_left]
Subgroup.quotientEquivProdOfLE'.description: This definition provides a constructive isomorphism between the quotient of a group by a smaller subgroup and the product of the quotient by a larger subgroup and the quotient of the larger subgroup by the smaller one.

add_subgroup.quotient_equiv_sum_of_le'.fullDefinition: def quotientEquivProdOfLE' (h_le : s ≤ t) (f : α ⧸ t → α)     (hf : Function.RightInverse f QuotientGroup.mk) : α ⧸ s ≃ (α ⧸ t) × t ⧸ s.subgroupOf t where   toFun a :=     ⟨a.map' id fun b c h => leftRel_apply.mpr (h_le (leftRel_apply.mp h)),       a.map' (fun g : α => ⟨(f (Quotient.mk'' g))⁻¹ * g, leftRel_apply.mp (Quotient.exact' (hf g))⟩)         fun b c h => by         rw [leftRel_apply]         change ((f b)⁻¹ * b)⁻¹ * ((f c)⁻¹ * c) ∈ s         have key : f b = f c :=           congr_arg f (Quotient.sound' (leftRel_apply.mpr (h_le (leftRel_apply.mp h))))         rwa [key, mul_inv_rev, inv_inv, mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel_left, ← leftRel_apply]⟩   invFun a := by     refine a.2.map' (fun (b : { x // x ∈ t}) => f a.1 * b) fun b c h => by       rw [leftRel_apply] at h ⊢       change (f a.1 * b)⁻¹ * (f a.1 * c) ∈ s       rwa [mul_inv_rev, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel_left]   left_inv := by     refine Quotient.ind' fun a => ?_     simp_rw [Quotient.map'_mk'', id, mul_inv_cancel_left]   right_inv := by     refine Prod.rec ?_     refine Quotient.ind' fun a => ?_     refine Quotient.ind' fun b => ?_     have key : Quotient.mk'' (f (Quotient.mk'' a) * b) = Quotient.mk'' a :=       (QuotientGroup.mk_mul_of_mem (f a) b.2).trans (hf a)     simp_rw [Quotient.map'_mk'', id, key, inv_mul_cancel_left]

QuotientGroup.preimageMkEquivSubgroupPro.comment:
If `s` is a subgroup of the group `α`, and `t` is a subset of `α ⧸ s`, then there is a
(typically non-canonical) bijection between the preimage of `t` in `α` and the product `s × t`.

QuotientGroup.preimageMkEquivSubgroupPro.fullDefinition: noncomputable def preimageMkEquivSubgroupProdSet (s : Subgroup α) (t : Set (α ⧸ s)) :     QuotientGroup.mk ⁻¹' t ≃ s × t where   toFun a :=     ⟨⟨((Quotient.out' (QuotientGroup.mk a)) : α)⁻¹ * a,         leftRel_apply.mp (@Quotient.exact' _ (leftRel s) _ _ <| Quotient.out_eq' _)⟩,       ⟨QuotientGroup.mk a, a.2⟩⟩   invFun a :=     ⟨Quotient.out' a.2.1 * a.1.1,       show QuotientGroup.mk _ ∈ t by         rw [mk_mul_of_mem _ a.1.2, out_eq']         exact a.2.2⟩   left_inv := fun ⟨a, ha⟩ => Subtype.eq <| show _ * _ = a by simp   right_inv := fun ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨x, hx⟩⟩ => by ext <;> simp [ha]

QuotientGroup.con.comment: The congruence relation generated by a normal subgroup.

explanatories.QuotientGroup.leftRel: This definition describes an equivalence relation that organizes a group into partitions based on the left cosets formed by a specific subgroup.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.leftRel_eq: This theorem defines the equivalence relation for the quotient group such that two elements are equivalent if the product of the inverse of one and the other belongs to the specified subgroup.
explanatories.mul_inv_rev: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the product of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the product of their individual inverses in reverse order.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.inv_mul_cancel_left: This theorem shows that in a group, the product of the inverse of an element and the product of that element with another element equals the other element itself.
explanatories.Subgroup.mul_mem: This theorem states that a subgroup is closed under multiplication, meaning that if two elements belong to the subgroup, their product also belongs to the subgroup.
explanatories.Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem: This theorem asserts that if a subgroup is normal and an element belongs to that subgroup, then conjugating that element by any group element will also result in an element that remains within the subgroup.

QuotientGroup.equivQuotientSubgroupOfOfE.comment:
Let `A', A, B', B` be subgroups of `G`.
If `A' = B'` and `A = B`, then the quotients `A / (A' ⊓ A)` and `B / (B' ⊓ B)` are isomorphic.

Applying this equiv is nicer than rewriting along the equalities, since the type of
`(A'.subgroupOf A : Subgroup A)` depends on `A`.

QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom.comment: The map of quotients by powers of an integer induced by a group homomorphism.

explanatories.MonoidHom.comp: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

explanatories.QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff: The theorem states that an element in a group is equal to the identity if and only if it belongs to the corresponding normal subgroup.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Con.lift: This definition describes a homomorphism on the quotient of a monoid, which is induced by a given homomorphism that remains constant across the equivalence classes defined by a particular congruence relation.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.lift: The definition describes how a group homomorphism can be lifted from a group to its quotient by a normal subgroup if the subgroup is contained in the kernel of the homomorphism.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.lift: The definition describes how a group homomorphism can be lifted from a group to its quotient by a normal subgroup if the subgroup is contained in the kernel of the homomorphism.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.map_zpow: This theorem asserts that group homomorphisms preserve the operation of taking integer powers in their algebraic structures.
explanatories.zpowGroupHom_apply: This theorem states that the application of the morphism that raises elements of a division commutative monoid to their integer power equals the result of raising those elements to that integer power directly.

QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom.fullDefinition: def homQuotientZPowOfHom :     A ⧸ (zpowGroupHom n : A →* A).range →* B ⧸ (zpowGroupHom n : B →* B).range :=   lift _ ((mk' _).comp f) fun g ⟨h, (hg : h ^ n = g)⟩ =>     (eq_one_iff _).mpr ⟨f h, by       simp only [← hg, map_zpow, zpowGroupHom_apply]⟩
QuotientGroup.homQuotientZPowOfHom.description: This definition describes a group homomorphism that maps the quotient of one commutative group by the range of element powers to the quotient of another commutative group by the same range.

explanatories.Set.Finite: A set is considered finite if there exists a natural number that demonstrates its equivalence to a finite set of natural numbers.
explanatories.nonempty_fintype: This theorem states that if a type is finite, then it must also have at least one finite enumeration.
explanatories.Finset.univ: This definition represents the universal finite set of a type that is finitely enumerable.
explanatories.Finset.coe_univ: This theorem shows that the universal finite set, when viewed as a set, is equal to the universal set of the underlying type that is finitely enumerable.
explanatories.Submonoid.closure_univ: The closure of the universal set in a multiplicative monoid is the top submonoid of that monoid.
explanatories.AddMonoid.fg_of_finite: Any finite monoid is also finitely generated.

explanatories.Subgroup.FG: A subgroup is considered finitely generated if it can be formed by the closure of a finite subset of elements from the group.
explanatories.Subgroup.closure_univ: This theorem states that the closure of the universal set in a group is equal to the entire group itself, indicating that all elements of the group can be generated from the universal set.

explanatories.Subgroup.coeSubtype: This theorem confirms that the canonical map from a subgroup to its associated subtype is equivalent to the standard value function of the subtype.
explanatories.Subgroup.closure_preimage_eq_top: This theorem asserts that the closure of the preimage of a set under the closure of that set is equal to the entire group.

explanatories.zsmul_eq_mul: This theorem states that the scalar multiplication of an element in a non-associative ring by an integer is equivalent to multiplying the element by the integer's image as an element of the ring.
explanatories.Int.cast_commute: This theorem states that elements of the form of integers commute with any element of a non-associative ring.
explanatories.Commute.eq: This theorem establishes that if two elements commute under multiplication, then the multiplication of those elements is equal regardless of their order.
explanatories.div_mul_cancel₀: This theorem states that in a group with zero, multiplying an element by a non-zero divisor yields the original element.
explanatories.Int.cast_ne_zero: This theorem asserts that an integer is non-zero if and only if its image under the homomorphism to an additive group is also non-zero, given that the group has characteristic zero and an additive identity.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

divisibleByIntOfCharZero.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) divisibleByIntOfCharZero {𝕜} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [CharZero 𝕜] :     DivisibleBy 𝕜 ℤ where   div q n := q / n   div_zero q := by norm_num   div_cancel {n} q hn := by     rw [zsmul_eq_mul, (Int.cast_commute n _).eq, div_mul_cancel₀ q (Int.cast_ne_zero.mpr hn)]
divisibleByIntOfCharZero.description: This definition states that a division ring with characteristic zero is divisible by the integers, meaning for every element in the division ring, there exists a counterpart in the integers such that division can be performed smoothly.

Group.rootableByIntOfRootableByNat.fullDefinition: def rootableByIntOfRootableByNat [RootableBy A ℕ] : RootableBy A ℤ where   root a z :=     match z with     | (n : ℕ) => RootableBy.root a n     | -[n+1] => (RootableBy.root a (n + 1))⁻¹   root_zero a := RootableBy.root_zero a   root_cancel {n} a hn := by     induction n     · change RootableBy.root a _ ^ _ = a       norm_num       rw [RootableBy.root_cancel]       rw [Int.ofNat_eq_coe] at hn       exact mod_cast hn     · change (RootableBy.root a _)⁻¹ ^ _ = a       norm_num       rw [RootableBy.root_cancel]       norm_num
Group.rootableByIntOfRootableByNat.description: This definition indicates that a group that can be rooted by natural numbers can also be rooted by integers, establishing a relationship between the two types of rootability.
