  [Monoid B] [Pow A α] [Pow B α] [RootableBy A α] (f : A → B) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
  (hpow : ∀ (a : A) (n : α), f (a ^ n) = f a ^ n) : RootableBy B α
Function.Surjective.rootableBy.comment: If `f : A → B` is a surjective homomorphism and `A` is `α`-rootable, then `B` is also `α`-rootable.

explanatories.RootableBy.root: This definition establishes a function that associates each element of a monoid with a corresponding root in a specified power structure, subject to certain conditions of existence and properties.
explanatories.RootableBy.root_cancel: This theorem asserts that for a non-zero exponent in a given power structure, raising the root of an element in a monoid to that exponent retrieves the original element.
explanatories.rootableByOfPowLeftSurj: This definition establishes that a monoid is rootable for a given power structure if the function that raises elements to any non-zero exponent is surjective.

Function.Surjective.rootableBy.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Function.Surjective.rootableBy (hf : Function.Surjective f)     (hpow : ∀ (a : A) (n : α), f (a ^ n) = f a ^ n) : RootableBy B α :=   rootableByOfPowLeftSurj _ _ fun {n} hn x =>     let ⟨y, hy⟩ := hf x     ⟨f <| RootableBy.root y n,       (by rw [← hpow (RootableBy.root y n) n, RootableBy.root_cancel _ hn, hy] : _ ^ n = x)⟩
Function.Surjective.rootableBy.description: This definition asserts that if a surjective homomorphism exists between two monoids and the first monoid is rootable by a specific power structure, then the second monoid inherits the property of being rootable by the same power structure.

PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup.fullDefinition: def equivPresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) (e : α ≃ β) :     PresentedGroup rels ≃* PresentedGroup (FreeGroup.freeGroupCongr e '' rels) :=   QuotientGroup.congr (Subgroup.normalClosure rels)     (Subgroup.normalClosure ((FreeGroup.freeGroupCongr e) '' rels)) (FreeGroup.freeGroupCongr e)     (Subgroup.map_normalClosure rels (FreeGroup.freeGroupCongr e).toMonoidHom       (FreeGroup.freeGroupCongr e).surjective)

explanatories.IsOfFinOrder.orderOf_pos: This theorem asserts that if an element in a monoid has finite order, then its order is a positive integer.
explanatories.pow_orderOf_eq_one: This theorem states that raising an element in a monoid to the power of its order results in the identity element of the monoid.
explanatories.pow_succ': This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one plus a natural number is equivalent to multiplying the element by itself raised to the power of that natural number.
explanatories.tsub_add_cancel_of_le: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another in an ordered structure, then subtracting the smaller element from the larger element and adding it back to the smaller element will yield the larger element.
explanatories.pow_succ: This theorem expresses that raising an element in a monoid to a successor exponent is equivalent to multiplying the element raised to the previous exponent by the element itself.

IsOfFinOrder.unit.fullDefinition: def IsOfFinOrder.unit {M} [Monoid M] {x : M} (hx : IsOfFinOrder x) : Mˣ := ⟨x, x ^ (orderOf x - 1),   by rw [← _root_.pow_succ', tsub_add_cancel_of_le (by exact hx.orderOf_pos), pow_orderOf_eq_one],   by rw [← _root_.pow_succ, tsub_add_cancel_of_le (by exact hx.orderOf_pos), pow_orderOf_eq_one]⟩
IsOfFinOrder.unit.description: This definition implies that if an element in a monoid has a finite order, then it is a unit, meaning it has a multiplicative inverse.

explanatories.Fin.ext: If two finite numbers have equal natural number representations, then they are equal.

explanatories.Nat.mod_lt: The remainder of a natural number when divided by a positive natural number is always less than the divisor.
explanatories.Subtype.eq: If two elements of a subtype have the same underlying value, then they are considered equal as elements of that subtype.
explanatories.Finset.ext: This theorem states that two finite sets are considered equal if they contain exactly the same elements.

finEquivMultiples.fullDefinition: noncomputable def finEquivPowers (x : G) (hx : IsOfFinOrder x) : Fin (orderOf x) ≃ powers x :=   Equiv.ofBijective (fun n ↦ ⟨x ^ (n : ℕ), ⟨n, rfl⟩⟩) ⟨fun ⟨_, h₁⟩ ⟨_, h₂⟩ ij ↦     Fin.ext (pow_injOn_Iio_orderOf h₁ h₂ (Subtype.mk_eq_mk.1 ij)), fun ⟨_, i, rfl⟩ ↦       ⟨⟨i % orderOf x, mod_lt _ hx.orderOf_pos⟩, Subtype.eq <| pow_mod_orderOf _ _⟩⟩

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Dvd.dvd.trans: This theorem establishes that if one element divides a second element and the second element divides a third element within a semigroup, then the first element also divides the third element.
explanatories.finEquivPowers: This definition describes a bijection between the finite ordinal type corresponding to the order of an element in a left-canceling monoid and the submonoid generated by its powers.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.

explanatories.zpow_mul: In a division monoid, raising an element to the product of two integers equals raising that element to the first integer and then raising the result to the second integer.
explanatories.one_zpow: Raising the identity element to any integer power results in the identity element itself within a division monoid.

explanatories.Nat.gcdB: This definition refers to a function that calculates the second coefficient in the extended Euclidean algorithm expression for the greatest common divisor of two natural numbers.
explanatories.Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab: This theorem establishes that the greatest common divisor of two natural numbers can be expressed as a linear combination of those numbers, using specific coefficients determined by the extended Euclidean algorithm.

explanatories.Set.Finite: A set is considered finite if there exists a natural number that demonstrates its equivalence to a finite set of natural numbers.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.orderOf_pos: This theorem states that in a finite left-canceling monoid, the order of any element is always a positive integer.
explanatories.submonoidOfIdempotent: This definition states that a non-empty idempotent subset of a finite cancellative monoid forms a submonoid.
explanatories.pow_sub: In a group, raising an element to the power of the difference between two non-negative integers can be expressed as the product of that element raised to the higher power and the inverse of its lower power.
explanatories.pow_mem: If an element belongs to a submonoid, all its integer powers also belong to that submonoid.

addSubgroupOfIdempotent.fullDefinition: def subgroupOfIdempotent {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (S : Set G) (hS1 : S.Nonempty)     (hS2 : S * S = S) : Subgroup G :=   { submonoidOfIdempotent S hS1 hS2 with     carrier := S     inv_mem' := fun {a} ha => show a⁻¹ ∈ submonoidOfIdempotent S hS1 hS2 by       rw [← one_mul a⁻¹, ← pow_one a, ← pow_orderOf_eq_one a, ← pow_sub a (orderOf_pos a)]       exact pow_mem ha (orderOf a - 1) }
addSubgroupOfIdempotent.description: A nonempty idempotent subset of a finite group qualifies as a subgroup.

powCardSubgroup.code: powCardSubgroup.{u_6} {G : Type u_6} [Group G] [Fintype G] (S : Set G) (hS : S.Nonempty) : Subgroup G
powCardSubgroup.comment: If `S` is a nonempty subset of a finite group `G`, then `S ^ |G|` is a subgroup

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.IsOfFinAddOrder.apply: This theorem states that if an element is of finite order in a direct product of monoids, then each component of that element is also of finite order.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Nat.card: This definition assigns a natural number representing the cardinality of a type, with the convention that infinite types are assigned the value zero.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.Subgroup.one_mem: This theorem asserts that the identity element of a group is contained in any subgroup of that group.
explanatories.pow_card_eq_one: This theorem states that raising an element in a finite group to the power equal to the cardinality of the group results in the identity element of the group.
explanatories.Set.pow_mem_pow: The theorem states that if an element belongs to a set in a monoid, then its powers also belong to the n-th power of that set.
explanatories.subgroupOfIdempotent: A nonempty idempotent subset of a finite group qualifies as a subgroup.
explanatories.Set.eq_of_subset_of_card_le: If one finite set is a subset of another finite set and the latter has less than or equal to the cardinality of the former, then the two sets must be equal.
explanatories.Set.subset_mul_left: The theorem states that if one set is non-empty and contains the multiplicative identity, then any subset of that set, when multiplied by the non-empty set, is included in the resulting set.
explanatories.ge_of_eq: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is greater than or equal to the other.
explanatories.Group.card_pow_eq_card_pow_card_univ: The theorem states that if the cardinality of a group is finite and less than or equal to a natural number, then the cardinality of the k-th power of a subset equals the cardinality of that subset raised to the cardinality of the group.
explanatories.le_add_self: This theorem asserts that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, any element is less than or equal to the sum of itself and another element.

powCardSubgroup.fullDefinition: def powCardSubgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (S : Set G) (hS : S.Nonempty) : Subgroup G :=   have one_mem : (1 : G) ∈ S ^ Fintype.card G := by     obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hS     rw [← pow_card_eq_one]     exact Set.pow_mem_pow ha (Fintype.card G)   subgroupOfIdempotent (S ^ Fintype.card G) ⟨1, one_mem⟩ <| by     classical     apply (Set.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (Set.subset_mul_left _ one_mem) (ge_of_eq _)).symm     simp_rw [← pow_add,         Group.card_pow_eq_card_pow_card_univ S (Fintype.card G + Fintype.card G) le_add_self]
powCardSubgroup.description: This definition states that a nonempty subset of a finite group generates a subgroup formed by taking all possible products of elements raised to the group's order.

free_abelian_group.punit_equiv.fullDefinition: def punitEquiv (T : Type*) [Unique T] : FreeAbelianGroup T ≃+ ℤ where   toFun := FreeAbelianGroup.lift fun _ ↦ (1 : ℤ)   invFun n := n • of Inhabited.default   left_inv z := FreeAbelianGroup.induction_on z     (by simp only [zero_smul, AddMonoidHom.map_zero])     (Unique.forall_iff.2 <| by simp only [one_smul, lift.of]) (Unique.forall_iff.2 <| by simp)     fun x y hx hy ↦ by       simp only [AddMonoidHom.map_add, add_smul] at *       rw [hx, hy]   right_inv n := by     rw [AddMonoidHom.map_zsmul, lift.of]     exact zsmul_int_one n   map_add' := AddMonoidHom.map_add _

CoxeterSystem.lift.fullDefinition: def lift {G : Type*} [Monoid G] : {f : B → G // IsLiftable M f} ≃ (W →* G) where   toFun f := MonoidHom.comp (Units.coeHom G) (cs.groupLift     (show ∀ i i', ((restrictUnit f.property) i * (restrictUnit f.property) i') ^ M i i' = 1 from       fun i i' ↦ Units.ext (f.property i i')))   invFun ι := ⟨ι ∘ cs.simple, fun i i' ↦ by     rw [comp_apply, comp_apply, ← map_mul, ← map_pow, simple_mul_simple_pow, map_one]⟩   left_inv f := by     ext i     simp only [MonoidHom.comp_apply, comp_apply, mem_setOf_eq, groupLift, simple]     rw [← MonoidHom.toFun_eq_coe, toMonoidHom_apply_symm_apply, PresentedGroup.toGroup.of,       OneHom.toFun_eq_coe, MonoidHom.toOneHom_coe, Units.coeHom_apply, restrictUnit]   right_inv ι := by     apply cs.ext_simple     intro i     dsimp only     rw [groupLift, simple, MonoidHom.comp_apply, MonoidHom.comp_apply, toMonoidHom_apply_symm_apply,       PresentedGroup.toGroup.of, CoxeterSystem.restrictUnit, Units.coeHom_apply]     simp only [comp_apply, simple]

  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) : W →* Multiplicative (ZMod 2)
CoxeterSystem.lengthParity.comment:
The homomorphism that sends each element `w : W` to the parity of the length of `w`.
(See `lengthParity_eq_ofAdd_length`.)

explanatories.Multiplicative: This definition indicates that a multiplicative structure can be derived from a type that primarily has an additive structure.
explanatories.ZMod: This definition introduces the type representing integers under modulo operation for a given natural number.
explanatories.CoxeterSystem.lift: This definition establishes a correspondence between functions that satisfy Coxeter relations and monoid homomorphisms to a given monoid.
explanatories.Multiplicative.ofAdd: This definition provides a way to reinterpret an element from a type with an additive structure as an element of the corresponding type with a multiplicative structure.
explanatories.CoxeterMatrix.IsLiftable: This definition states the condition under which a function from elements of a type to a monoid satisfies the Coxeter relations defined by a corresponding matrix.
explanatories.ofAdd_add: This theorem states that for a type equipped with an additive structure, the operation corresponding to the sum of two elements is equal to the product of their respective additive representations.

CoxeterSystem.lengthParity.fullDefinition: def lengthParity : W →* Multiplicative (ZMod 2) := cs.lift ⟨fun _ ↦ Multiplicative.ofAdd 1, by   simp_rw [CoxeterMatrix.IsLiftable, ← ofAdd_add, (by decide : (1 + 1 : ZMod 2) = 0)]   simp⟩
CoxeterSystem.lengthParity.description: This definition introduces a homomorphism that assigns each group element the parity of its length within a Coxeter system.

CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.code:
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (t : W) : Prop
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.comment:
`t : W` is a *reflection* of the Coxeter system `cs` if it is of the form
$w s_i w^{-1}$, where $w \in W$ and $s_i$ is a simple reflection.
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.fullDefinition: def IsReflection (t : W) : Prop := ∃ w i, t = w * s i * w⁻¹
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.description: This definition characterizes an element of a Coxeter system as a reflection if it can be expressed as a product involving a simple reflection and an arbitrary element of the group.

CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.inv.code:

  {cs : CoxeterSystem M W} {t : W} (ht : cs.IsReflection t) : t⁻¹ = t
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.inv.description: This theorem establishes that if an element is a reflection in a Coxeter system, then its inverse is equal to itself.

CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.conj.code:
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.conj.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  {cs : CoxeterSystem M W} {t : W} (ht : cs.IsReflection t) (w : W) : cs.IsReflection (w * t * w⁻¹)
CoxeterSystem.IsReflection.conj.description: This theorem asserts that if an element is a reflection in a Coxeter system, then conjugating that element by any other group element also results in a reflection within the same system.

CoxeterSystem.IsRightInversion.code:
CoxeterSystem.IsRightInversion.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (w t : W) : Prop
CoxeterSystem.IsRightInversion.comment:
The proposition that `t` is a right inversion of `w`; i.e., `t` is a reflection and
$\ell (w t) < \ell(w)$.

explanatories.CoxeterSystem.IsReflection: This definition characterizes an element of a Coxeter system as a reflection if it can be expressed as a product involving a simple reflection and an arbitrary element of the group.

CoxeterSystem.IsRightInversion.fullDefinition: def IsRightInversion (w t : W) : Prop := cs.IsReflection t ∧ ℓ (w * t) < ℓ w
CoxeterSystem.IsRightInversion.description: This definition states that a given element in a Coxeter system is considered a right inversion of another if it acts as a reflection and reduces the length of their product.

CoxeterSystem.IsLeftInversion.code:
CoxeterSystem.IsLeftInversion.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (w t : W) : Prop
CoxeterSystem.IsLeftInversion.comment:
The proposition that `t` is a left inversion of `w`; i.e., `t` is a reflection and
$\ell (t w) < \ell(w)$.

explanatories.CoxeterSystem.IsReflection: This definition characterizes an element of a Coxeter system as a reflection if it can be expressed as a product involving a simple reflection and an arbitrary element of the group.

CoxeterSystem.IsLeftInversion.fullDefinition: def IsLeftInversion (w t : W) : Prop := cs.IsReflection t ∧ ℓ (t * w) < ℓ w
CoxeterSystem.IsLeftInversion.description: This definition indicates that an element in a Coxeter system is considered a left inversion of another element if it acts as a reflection and the length of their product is less than the length of the original element.

CoxeterSystem.rightInvSeq.code:
CoxeterSystem.rightInvSeq.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (ω : List B) : List W
CoxeterSystem.rightInvSeq.comment:
The right inversion sequence of `ω`. The right inversion sequence of a word
$s_{i_1} \cdots s_{i_\ell}$ is the sequence
$$s_{i_\ell}\cdots s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}, \ldots,
    s_{i_{\ell}}s_{i_{\ell - 1}}s_{i_{\ell - 2}}s_{i_{\ell - 1}}s_{i_\ell}, \ldots,
    s_{i_{\ell}}s_{i_{\ell - 1}}s_{i_\ell}, s_{i_\ell}.$$
CoxeterSystem.rightInvSeq.fullDefinition: def rightInvSeq (ω : List B) : List W :=   match ω with   | []          => []   | i :: ω      => (π ω)⁻¹ * (s i) * (π ω) :: rightInvSeq ω
CoxeterSystem.rightInvSeq.description: This definition describes the right inversion sequence of a word in a Coxeter system as a list of elements generated by systematically reflecting the components of the word in reverse order while incorporating repetitions of the last element throughout the sequence.

CoxeterSystem.leftInvSeq.code:
CoxeterSystem.leftInvSeq.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B}
  (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (ω : List B) : List W
CoxeterSystem.leftInvSeq.comment:
The left inversion sequence of `ω`. The left inversion sequence of a word
$s_{i_1} \cdots s_{i_\ell}$ is the sequence
$$s_{i_1}, s_{i_1}s_{i_2}s_{i_1}, s_{i_1}s_{i_2}s_{i_3}s_{i_2}s_{i_1}, \ldots,
    s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}\cdots s_{i_1}.$$

Commute.orderOf_mul_pow_eq_lcm.code:
Commute.orderOf_mul_pow_eq_lcm.{u} {G : Type u} [Monoid G] {x y : G} (h : Commute x y) (hx : orderOf x ≠ 0)
  (hy : orderOf y ≠ 0) :
  orderOf
      (x ^ (orderOf x / (orderOf x).factorizationLCMLeft (orderOf y)) *
        y ^ (orderOf y / (orderOf x).factorizationLCMRight (orderOf y))) =
    (orderOf x).lcm (orderOf y)
Commute.orderOf_mul_pow_eq_lcm.comment:
If two commuting elements `x` and `y` of a monoid have order `n` and `m`, there is an element
of order `lcm n m`. The result actually gives an explicit (computable) element, written as the
product of a power of `x` and a power of `y`. See also the result below if you don't need the
explicit formula.

DihedralGroup.OddCommuteEquiv.fullDefinition: def OddCommuteEquiv (hn : Odd n) : { p : DihedralGroup n × DihedralGroup n // Commute p.1 p.2 } ≃     ZMod n ⊕ ZMod n ⊕ ZMod n ⊕ ZMod n × ZMod n :=   let u := ZMod.unitOfCoprime 2 (Nat.prime_two.coprime_iff_not_dvd.mpr hn.not_two_dvd_nat)   have hu : ∀ a : ZMod n, a + a = 0 ↔ a = 0 := fun a => ZMod.add_self_eq_zero_iff_eq_zero hn   { toFun := fun       | ⟨⟨sr i, r _⟩, _⟩ => Sum.inl i       | ⟨⟨r _, sr j⟩, _⟩ => Sum.inr (Sum.inl j)       | ⟨⟨sr i, sr j⟩, _⟩ => Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (i + j)))       | ⟨⟨r i, r j⟩, _⟩ => Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr ⟨i, j⟩))     invFun := fun       | .inl i => ⟨⟨sr i, r 0⟩, congrArg sr ((add_zero i).trans (sub_zero i).symm)⟩       | .inr (.inl j) => ⟨⟨r 0, sr j⟩, congrArg sr ((sub_zero j).trans (add_zero j).symm)⟩       | .inr (.inr (.inl k)) => ⟨⟨sr (u⁻¹ * k), sr (u⁻¹ * k)⟩, rfl⟩       | .inr (.inr (.inr ⟨i, j⟩)) => ⟨⟨r i, r j⟩, congrArg r (add_comm i j)⟩     left_inv := fun       | ⟨⟨r i, r j⟩, h⟩ => rfl       | ⟨⟨r i, sr j⟩, h⟩ => by         simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, neg_eq_iff_add_eq_zero, hu, eq_comm (a := i) (b := 0)] using h.eq       | ⟨⟨sr i, r j⟩, h⟩ => by         simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero, hu, eq_comm (a := j) (b := 0)] using h.eq       | ⟨⟨sr i, sr j⟩, h⟩ => by         replace h := r.inj h         rw [← neg_sub, neg_eq_iff_add_eq_zero, hu, sub_eq_zero] at h         rw [Subtype.ext_iff, Prod.ext_iff, sr.injEq, sr.injEq, h, and_self, ← two_mul]         exact u.inv_mul_cancel_left j     right_inv := fun       | .inl i => rfl       | .inr (.inl j) => rfl       | .inr (.inr (.inl k)) =>         congrArg (Sum.inr ∘ Sum.inr ∘ Sum.inl) <| two_mul (u⁻¹ * k) ▸ u.mul_inv_cancel_left k       | .inr (.inr (.inr ⟨i, j⟩)) => rfl }

explanatories.Subtype.ext_iff: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their corresponding values in the underlying set are equal.
explanatories.alternatingGroup.normalClosure_swap_mul_: This theorem asserts that the normal closure of the permutation consisting of two swaps in the alternating group of five elements is the entire group.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.sum_cycleType: The sum of the lengths of the cycles in a permutation equals the number of elements in its support.

explanatories.Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.cycleType: The cycle type of a permutation that is a cycle is equal to a multiset containing the size of its support.
explanatories.alternatingGroup.isConj_swap_mul_swap_of: This theorem demonstrates that any non-identity permutation in a specific alternating group, composed exclusively of 2-cycles, is conjugate to a particular product of two swaps.
explanatories.or_not: This theorem states that for any proposition, either the proposition is true or its negation is true, thereby establishing the principle of excluded middle.
explanatories.Or.imp: The theorem states that if one can derive a consequence from either of two propositions and at least one of those propositions holds, then it is possible to conclude at least one of the consequences also holds.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall: This theorem states that a subgroup is trivial if and only if every element in the subgroup is the identity element of the group.
explanatories.ge_of_eq: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is greater than or equal to the other.
explanatories.IsConj.normalClosure_eq_top_of: This theorem states that if two elements of a normal subgroup are conjugate and the normal closure of one is the entire group, then the normal closure of the other element is also the entire group.
explanatories.lt_of_le_of_ne: This theorem states that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and they are not equal, then the first element is strictly less than the second.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Multiset.exists_cons_of_mem: This theorem asserts that if an element is a member of a multiset, then there exists another multiset such that the original multiset can be expressed as the addition of that element to the new multiset.
explanatories.Multiset.sum_cons: The sum of a multiset formed by adding an element to another multiset is equal to the sum of the added element and the sum of the original multiset.
explanatories.le_add_right: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, if one element is less than or equal to another, then it is also less than or equal to the sum of that element and any third element.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.

explanatories.Odd: A number in a semiring is considered odd if it can be expressed as one more than twice another number.
explanatories.cycleType_finRotate: This theorem establishes that the cycle structure of the rotation permutation on a set with two more elements consists of a single cycle that includes all elements.

alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five.fullDefinition: instance isSimpleGroup_five : IsSimpleGroup (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) :=   ⟨fun H => by     intro Hn     refine or_not.imp id fun Hb => ?_     rw [eq_bot_iff_forall] at Hb     push_neg at Hb     obtain ⟨⟨g, gA⟩, gH, g1⟩ : ∃ x : ↥(alternatingGroup (Fin 5)), x ∈ H ∧ x ≠ 1 := Hb     -- `g` is a non-identity alternating permutation in a normal subgroup `H` of $A_5$.     rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, ← Set.singleton_subset_iff] at gH     refine eq_top_iff.2 (le_trans (ge_of_eq ?_) (normalClosure_le_normal gH))     -- It suffices to show that the normal closure of `g` in $A_5$ is $A_5$.     by_cases h2 : ∀ n ∈ g.cycleType, n = 2     -- If the cycle decomposition of `g` consists entirely of swaps, then the cycle type is $(2,2)$.     -- This means that it is conjugate to $(04)(13)$, whose normal closure is $A_5$.     · rw [Ne, Subtype.ext_iff] at g1       exact         (isConj_swap_mul_swap_of_cycleType_two gA g1 h2).normalClosure_eq_top_of           normalClosure_swap_mul_swap_five     push_neg at h2     obtain ⟨n, ng, n2⟩ : ∃ n : ℕ, n ∈ g.cycleType ∧ n ≠ 2 := h2     -- `n` is the size of a non-swap cycle in the decomposition of `g`.     have n2' : 2 < n := lt_of_le_of_ne (two_le_of_mem_cycleType ng) n2.symm     have n5 : n ≤ 5 := le_trans ?_ g.support.card_le_univ     -- We check that `2 < n ≤ 5`, so that `interval_cases` has a precise range to check.     swap     · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Multiset.exists_cons_of_mem ng       rw [← sum_cycleType, hm, Multiset.sum_cons]       exact le_add_right le_rfl     interval_cases n     -- This breaks into cases `n = 3`, `n = 4`, `n = 5`.     -- If `n = 3`, then `g` has a 3-cycle in its decomposition, so `g^2` is a 3-cycle.     -- `g^2` is in the normal closure of `g`, so that normal closure must be $A_5$.     · rw [eq_top_iff, ← (isThreeCycle_sq_of_three_mem_cycleType_five ng).alternating_normalClosure         (by rw [card_fin])]       refine normalClosure_le_normal ?_       rw [Set.singleton_subset_iff, SetLike.mem_coe]       have h := SetLike.mem_coe.1 (subset_normalClosure         (G := alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) (Set.mem_singleton ⟨g, gA⟩))       exact mul_mem h h     · -- The case `n = 4` leads to contradiction, as no element of $A_5$ includes a 4-cycle.       have con := mem_alternatingGroup.1 gA       rw [sign_of_cycleType, cycleType_of_card_le_mem_cycleType_add_two (by decide) ng] at con       have : Odd 5 := by decide       simp [this] at con     · -- If `n = 5`, then `g` is itself a 5-cycle, conjugate to `finRotate 5`.       refine (isConj_iff_cycleType_eq.2 ?_).normalClosure_eq_top_of normalClosure_finRotate_five       rw [cycleType_of_card_le_mem_cycleType_add_two (by decide) ng, cycleType_finRotate]⟩

Subgroup.isCyclic.fullDefinition: instance Subgroup.isCyclic {α : Type u} [Group α] [IsCyclic α] (H : Subgroup α) : IsCyclic H :=   haveI := Classical.propDecidable   let ⟨g, hg⟩ := IsCyclic.exists_generator (α := α)   if hx : ∃ x : α, x ∈ H ∧ x ≠ (1 : α) then     let ⟨x, hx₁, hx₂⟩ := hx     let ⟨k, hk⟩ := hg x     have hk : g ^ k = x := hk     have hex : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ g ^ n ∈ H :=       ⟨k.natAbs,         Nat.pos_of_ne_zero fun h => hx₂ <| by           rw [← hk, Int.natAbs_eq_zero.mp h, zpow_zero], by             cases' k with k k             · rw [Int.ofNat_eq_coe, Int.natAbs_cast k, ← zpow_natCast, ← Int.ofNat_eq_coe, hk]               exact hx₁             · rw [Int.natAbs_negSucc, ← Subgroup.inv_mem_iff H]; simp_all⟩     ⟨⟨⟨g ^ Nat.find hex, (Nat.find_spec hex).2⟩, fun ⟨x, hx⟩ =>         let ⟨k, hk⟩ := hg x         have hk : g ^ k = x := hk         have hk₂ : g ^ ((Nat.find hex : ℤ) * (k / Nat.find hex : ℤ)) ∈ H := by           rw [zpow_mul]           apply H.zpow_mem           exact mod_cast (Nat.find_spec hex).2         have hk₃ : g ^ (k % Nat.find hex : ℤ) ∈ H :=           (Subgroup.mul_mem_cancel_right H hk₂).1 <| by             rw [← zpow_add, Int.emod_add_ediv, hk]; exact hx         have hk₄ : k % Nat.find hex = (k % Nat.find hex).natAbs := by           rw [Int.natAbs_of_nonneg               (Int.emod_nonneg _ (Int.natCast_ne_zero_iff_pos.2 (Nat.find_spec hex).1))]         have hk₅ : g ^ (k % Nat.find hex).natAbs ∈ H := by rwa [← zpow_natCast, ← hk₄]         have hk₆ : (k % (Nat.find hex : ℤ)).natAbs = 0 :=           by_contradiction fun h =>             Nat.find_min hex               (Int.ofNat_lt.1 <| by                 rw [← hk₄]; exact Int.emod_lt_of_pos _ (Int.natCast_pos.2 (Nat.find_spec hex).1))               ⟨Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h, hk₅⟩         ⟨k / (Nat.find hex : ℤ),           Subtype.ext_iff_val.2             (by               suffices g ^ ((Nat.find hex : ℤ) * (k / Nat.find hex : ℤ)) = x by simpa [zpow_mul]               rw [Int.mul_ediv_cancel'                   (Int.dvd_of_emod_eq_zero (Int.natAbs_eq_zero.mp hk₆)),                 hk])⟩⟩⟩   else by     have : H = (⊥ : Subgroup α) :=       Subgroup.ext fun x =>         ⟨fun h => by simp at *; tauto, fun h => by rw [Subgroup.mem_bot.1 h]; exact H.one_mem⟩     subst this; infer_instance

explanatories.subsingleton_or_nontrivial: Every type is either a subsingleton or nontrivial.

IsSimpleGroup.isCyclic.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) isCyclic : IsCyclic α := by   cases' subsingleton_or_nontrivial α with hi hi <;> haveI := hi   · apply isCyclic_of_subsingleton   · obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_ne (1 : α)     refine ⟨⟨g, fun x => ?_⟩⟩     cases' IsSimpleOrder.eq_bot_or_eq_top (Subgroup.zpowers g) with hb ht     · exfalso       apply hg       rw [← Subgroup.mem_bot, ← hb]       apply Subgroup.mem_zpowers     · rw [ht]       apply Subgroup.mem_top

DihedralGroup.reciprocalFactors.fullDefinition: def reciprocalFactors (n : ℕ) : List ℕ :=   if h0 : n = 0 then [0]   else if h1 : n = 1 then []   else if Even n then     3 :: reciprocalFactors (n / 2)   else     n % 4 * n :: reciprocalFactors (n / 4 + 1)

DihedralGroup.reciprocalFactors.eq_1.code:
DihedralGroup.reciprocalFactors.eq_1 (n : ℕ) :
  reciprocalFactors n =
    if h0 : n = 0 then [0]
    else
      if h1 : n = 1 then []
      else if Even n then 3 :: reciprocalFactors (n / 2) else n % 4 * n :: reciprocalFactors (n / 4 + 1)

MonoidHom.commutatorMap.comment:
The commutator map `g ↦ g / φ g`. If `φ g = h * g * h⁻¹`, then `g / φ g` is exactly the
commutator `[g, h] = g * h * g⁻¹ * h⁻¹`.
MonoidHom.commutatorMap.fullDefinition: def commutatorMap [Div G] (g : G) := g / φ g

MonoidHom.FixedPointFree.fullDefinition: def FixedPointFree [One G] := ∀ g, φ g = g → g = 1
MonoidHom.FixedPointFree.description: This definition states that a function is considered fixed-point-free if the identity element is the only element that remains unchanged when the function is applied.

HNNExtension.con.fullDefinition: def HNNExtension.con (G : Type*) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G) (φ : A ≃* B) :     Con (G ∗ Multiplicative ℤ) :=   conGen (fun x y => ∃ (a : A),     x = inr (ofAdd 1) * inl (a : G) ∧     y = inl (φ a : G) * inr (ofAdd 1))
HNNExtension.con.description: The definition describes the construction of an HNN extension of a group by specifying the relation used to form this extension from the coproduct of the original group and the integers.

HNNExtension.code: HNNExtension.{u_1} (G : Type u_1) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G) (φ : ↥A ≃* ↥B) : Type u_1
HNNExtension.comment:
The HNN Extension of a group `G`, `HNNExtension G A B φ`. Given a group `G`, subgroups `A` and
`B` and an isomorphism `φ` of `A` and `B`, we adjoin a letter `t` to `G`, such that for
any `a ∈ A`, the conjugate of `of a` by `t` is `of (φ a)`, where `of` is the canonical
map from `G` into the `HNNExtension`.

HNNExtension.toSubgroup.comment:
To avoid duplicating code, we define `toSubgroup A B u` and `toSubgroupEquiv u`
where `u : ℤˣ` is `1` or `-1`. `toSubgroup A B u` is `A` when `u = 1` and `B` when `u = -1`,
and `toSubgroupEquiv` is `φ` when `u = 1` and `φ⁻¹` when `u = -1`. `toSubgroup u` is the subgroup
such that for any `a ∈ toSubgroup u`, `t ^ (u : ℤ) * a = toSubgroupEquiv a * t ^ (u : ℤ)`.

where `u : ℤˣ` is `1` or `-1`. `toSubgroup A B u` is `A` when `u = 1` and `B` when `u = -1`,
and `toSubgroupEquiv` is the group ismorphism from `toSubgroup A B u` to `toSubgroup A B (-u)`.

HNNExtension.NormalWord.consRecOn.fullDefinition: def consRecOn {motive : NormalWord d → Sort*} (w : NormalWord d)     (ofGroup : ∀g, motive (ofGroup g))     (cons : ∀ (g : G) (u : ℤˣ) (w : NormalWord d) (h1 : w.head ∈ d.set u)       (h2 : ∀ u' ∈ Option.map Prod.fst w.toList.head?,         w.head ∈ toSubgroup A B u → u = u'),       motive w → motive (cons g u w h1 h2)) : motive w := by   rcases w with ⟨⟨g, l, chain⟩, mem_set⟩   induction l generalizing g with   | nil => exact ofGroup _   | cons a l ih =>     exact cons g a.1       { head := a.2         toList := l         mem_set := fun _ _ h => mem_set _ _ (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h),         chain := (List.chain'_cons'.1 chain).2 }       (mem_set a.1 a.2 (List.mem_cons_self _ _))       (by simpa using (List.chain'_cons'.1 chain).1)       (ih _ _ _)

  {d : TransversalPair G A B} (u : ℤˣ) (w : NormalWord d) :

Monoid.PushoutI.NormalWord.rcons.fullDefinition: noncomputable def rcons (i : ι) (p : Pair d i) : NormalWord d :=   letI n := (d.compl i).equiv p.head   let w := (Word.equivPair i).symm { p.toPair with head := n.2 }   { toWord := w     head := (MonoidHom.ofInjective (d.injective i)).symm n.1     normalized := fun i g hg => by         dsimp [w] at hg         rw [Word.equivPair_symm, Word.mem_rcons_iff] at hg         rcases hg with hg | ⟨_, rfl, rfl⟩         · exact p.normalized _ _ hg         · simp }

Monoid.PushoutI.NormalWord.equivPair.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equivPair (i) : NormalWord d ≃ Pair d i :=   letI toFun : NormalWord d → Pair d i :=     fun w =>       letI p := Word.equivPair i (CoprodI.of (φ i w.head) • w.toWord)       { toPair := p         normalized := fun j g hg => by           dsimp only [p] at hg           rw [Word.of_smul_def, ← Word.equivPair_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hg           dsimp at hg           exact w.normalized _ _ (Word.mem_of_mem_equivPair_tail _ hg) }   haveI leftInv : Function.LeftInverse (rcons i) toFun :=     fun w => ext_smul i <| by       simp only [rcons, Word.equivPair_symm,         Word.equivPair_smul_same, Word.equivPair_tail_eq_inv_smul, Word.rcons_eq_smul,         MonoidHom.apply_ofInjective_symm, equiv_fst_eq_mul_inv, mul_assoc, map_mul, map_inv,         mul_smul, inv_smul_smul, smul_inv_smul]   { toFun := toFun     invFun := rcons i     left_inv := leftInv     right_inv := fun _ => rcons_injective (leftInv _) }

Monoid.PushoutI.NormalWord.consRecOn.fullDefinition: noncomputable def consRecOn {motive : NormalWord d → Sort _} (w : NormalWord d)     (h_empty : motive empty)     (h_cons : ∀ (i : ι) (g : G i) (w : NormalWord d) (hmw : w.fstIdx ≠ some i)       (_hgn : g ∈ d.set i) (hgr : g ∉ (φ i).range) (_hw1 : w.head = 1),       motive w →  motive (cons g w hmw hgr))     (h_base : ∀ (h : H) (w : NormalWord d), w.head = 1 → motive w → motive       (base φ h • w)) : motive w := by   rcases w with ⟨w, head, h3⟩   convert h_base head ⟨w, 1, h3⟩ rfl ?_   · simp [base_smul_def]   · induction w using Word.consRecOn with     | h_empty => exact h_empty     | h_cons i g w h1 hg1 ih =>       convert h_cons i g ⟨w, 1, fun _ _ h => h3 _ _ (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h)⟩         h1 (h3 _ _ (List.mem_cons_self _ _)) ?_ rfl         (ih ?_)       · ext         simp only [Word.cons, Option.mem_def, cons, map_one, mul_one,           (equiv_snd_eq_self_iff_mem (d.compl i) (one_mem _)).2           (h3 _ _ (List.mem_cons_self _ _))]       · apply d.injective i         simp only [cons, equiv_fst_eq_mul_inv, MonoidHom.apply_ofInjective_symm,           map_one, mul_one, mul_right_inv, (equiv_snd_eq_self_iff_mem (d.compl i) (one_mem _)).2           (h3 _ _ (List.mem_cons_self _ _))]       · rwa [← SetLike.mem_coe,           ← coe_equiv_snd_eq_one_iff_mem (d.compl i) (d.one_mem _),           (equiv_snd_eq_self_iff_mem (d.compl i) (one_mem _)).2           (h3 _ _ (List.mem_cons_self _ _))]

Sylow.directProductOfNormal.fullDefinition: noncomputable def directProductOfNormal [Fintype G]     (hn : ∀ {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G), (↑P : Subgroup G).Normal) :     (∀ p : (card G).primeFactors, ∀ P : Sylow p G, (↑P : Subgroup G)) ≃* G := by   set ps := (Fintype.card G).primeFactors   -- “The” Sylow subgroup for p   let P : ∀ p, Sylow p G := default   have hcomm : Pairwise fun p₁ p₂ : ps => ∀ x y : G, x ∈ P p₁ → y ∈ P p₂ → Commute x y := by     rintro ⟨p₁, hp₁⟩ ⟨p₂, hp₂⟩ hne     haveI hp₁' := Fact.mk (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp₁)     haveI hp₂' := Fact.mk (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp₂)     have hne' : p₁ ≠ p₂ := by simpa using hne     apply Subgroup.commute_of_normal_of_disjoint _ _ (hn (P p₁)) (hn (P p₂))     apply IsPGroup.disjoint_of_ne p₁ p₂ hne' _ _ (P p₁).isPGroup' (P p₂).isPGroup'   refine MulEquiv.trans (N := ∀ p : ps, P p) ?_ ?_   -- There is only one Sylow subgroup for each p, so the inner product is trivial   · show (∀ p : ps, ∀ P : Sylow p G, P) ≃* ∀ p : ps, P p     -- here we need to help the elaborator with an explicit instantiation     apply @MulEquiv.piCongrRight ps (fun p => ∀ P : Sylow p G, P) (fun p => P p) _ _     rintro ⟨p, hp⟩     haveI hp' := Fact.mk (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp)     letI := unique_of_normal _ (hn (P p))     apply MulEquiv.piUnique   show (∀ p : ps, P p) ≃* G   apply MulEquiv.ofBijective (Subgroup.noncommPiCoprod hcomm)   apply (bijective_iff_injective_and_card _).mpr   constructor   · show Injective _     apply Subgroup.injective_noncommPiCoprod_of_independent     apply independent_of_coprime_order hcomm     rintro ⟨p₁, hp₁⟩ ⟨p₂, hp₂⟩ hne     haveI hp₁' := Fact.mk (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp₁)     haveI hp₂' := Fact.mk (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp₂)     have hne' : p₁ ≠ p₂ := by simpa using hne     apply IsPGroup.coprime_card_of_ne p₁ p₂ hne' _ _ (P p₁).isPGroup' (P p₂).isPGroup'   · show card (∀ p : ps, P p) = card G     calc       card (∀ p : ps, P p) = ∏ p : ps, card (P p) := Fintype.card_pi       _ = ∏ p : ps, p.1 ^ (card G).factorization p.1 := by         congr 1 with ⟨p, hp⟩         exact @card_eq_multiplicity _ _ _ p ⟨Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp⟩ (P p)       _ = ∏ p ∈ ps, p ^ (card G).factorization p :=         (Finset.prod_finset_coe (fun p => p ^ (card G).factorization p) _)       _ = (card G).factorization.prod (· ^ ·) := rfl       _ = card G := Nat.factorization_prod_pow_eq_self Fintype.card_ne_zero

CommMonoid.primaryComponent.comment: The `p`-primary component is the submonoid of elements with order prime-power of `p`.

explanatories.orderOf: This definition specifies the order of an element in a monoid, which is the smallest positive integer such that raising the element to that integer results in the identity element, or zero if the element has infinite order.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.pow_mul: This theorem states that for any element in a monoid, raising it to the product of two natural numbers is equivalent to first raising it to one of those numbers and then raising the result to the other number.
explanatories.exists_orderOf_eq_prime_pow_iff: This theorem states that an element in a monoid has an order equal to a prime power if and only if there exists a non-negative integer such that raising the element to that prime power results in the identity element.
explanatories.mul_pow: In a commutative monoid, the power of a product of two elements equals the product of their individual powers.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.one_pow: This theorem asserts that raising the multiplicative identity to any natural number results in the multiplicative identity itself.
explanatories.Monoid.one_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by one on the left side does not change the value of that element in a monoid.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.pow_zero: This theorem asserts that any element raised to the power of zero in a monoid equals the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.orderOf_one: This theorem states that the order of the identity element in a monoid is equal to one.
explanatories.Eq.mpr: If there is a proof of equality between two types, then this definition provides a way to convert an element of one type to an element of the other type.

CommMonoid.primaryComponent.fullDefinition: def primaryComponent : Submonoid G where   carrier := { g | ∃ n : ℕ, orderOf g = p ^ n }   one_mem' := ⟨0, by rw [pow_zero, orderOf_one]⟩   mul_mem' hg₁ hg₂ :=     exists_orderOf_eq_prime_pow_iff.mpr <| by       obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := exists_orderOf_eq_prime_pow_iff.mp hg₁       obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_orderOf_eq_prime_pow_iff.mp hg₂       exact         ⟨m + n, by           rw [mul_pow, pow_add, pow_mul, hm, one_pow, Monoid.one_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul, hn,             one_pow]⟩
CommMonoid.primaryComponent.description: The p-primary component of a commutative monoid consists of elements whose orders are powers of a prime number p.

Monoid.minOrder.comment:
The minimum order of a non-identity element. Also the minimum size of a nontrivial subgroup, see
`Monoid.le_minOrder_iff_forall_subgroup`. Returns `∞` if the monoid is torsion-free.

explanatories.IsOfFinOrder: This definition states that an element in a monoid is of finite order if there exists a positive integer such that raising the element to that integer results in the identity element of the monoid.

Monoid.minOrder_eq_top.description: The theorem establishes a relationship between the minimum order of elements in a monoid and the property of the monoid being torsion-free, indicating that the minimum order is infinite if and only if the monoid does not contain elements of finite order.

upperCentralSeriesStep.code: upperCentralSeriesStep.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] : Subgroup G
upperCentralSeriesStep.comment:
If `H` is a normal subgroup of `G`, then the set `{x : G | ∀ y : G, x*y*x⁻¹*y⁻¹ ∈ H}`
is a subgroup of `G` (because it is the preimage in `G` of the centre of the
quotient group `G/H`.)

explanatories.Subgroup.mul_mem: This theorem states that a subgroup is closed under multiplication, meaning that if two elements belong to the subgroup, their product also belongs to the subgroup.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.Subgroup.one_mem: This theorem asserts that the identity element of a group is contained in any subgroup of that group.
explanatories.inv_inv: This theorem demonstrates that taking the inverse of an element twice in a group retrieves the original element.
explanatories.Subgroup.Normal.mem_comm: This theorem establishes that in a normal subgroup, the product of two elements implies the reverse product is also contained in the subgroup.
explanatories.inferInstance: This function generates an instance of a type by utilizing typeclass inference, acting like an identity function but specifically aiming to construct values required for class instances.
explanatories.MulMemClass.mul_mem: This theorem states that a set defined by a multiplication property is closed under the operation of multiplication.

upperCentralSeriesStep.fullDefinition: def upperCentralSeriesStep : Subgroup G where   carrier := { x : G | ∀ y : G, x * y * x⁻¹ * y⁻¹ ∈ H }   one_mem' y := by simp [Subgroup.one_mem]   mul_mem' {a b ha hb y} := by     convert Subgroup.mul_mem _ (ha (b * y * b⁻¹)) (hb y) using 1     group   inv_mem' {x hx y} := by     specialize hx y⁻¹     rw [mul_assoc, inv_inv] at hx ⊢     exact Subgroup.Normal.mem_comm inferInstance hx
upperCentralSeriesStep.description: The step of the upper central series for a normal subgroup in a group is defined as the set of elements that commute with every group element up to the normal subgroup.

IsAscendingCentralSeries.code: IsAscendingCentralSeries.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (H : ℕ → Subgroup G) : Prop
IsAscendingCentralSeries.comment:
A sequence of subgroups of `G` is an ascending central series if `H 0` is trivial and
`⁅H (n + 1), G⁆ ⊆ H n` for all `n`. Note that we do not require that `H n = G` for some `n`.
IsAscendingCentralSeries.fullDefinition: def IsAscendingCentralSeries (H : ℕ → Subgroup G) : Prop :=   H 0 = ⊥ ∧ ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), x ∈ H (n + 1) → ∀ g, x * g * x⁻¹ * g⁻¹ ∈ H n
IsAscendingCentralSeries.description: A sequence of subgroups in a group is considered an ascending central series if the first subgroup is trivial and the commutator of each subsequent subgroup with the group is contained within the previous subgroup.

subgroup `K` which is a (right) complement of `H`.

EckmannHilton.commMonoid.fullDefinition: def commMonoid [h : MulOneClass X]     (distrib : ∀ a b c d, ((a * b) <m₁> c * d) = (a <m₁> c) * b <m₁> d) : CommMonoid X :=   { h with       mul_comm := (mul_comm h₁ MulOneClass.isUnital distrib).comm,       mul_assoc := (mul_assoc h₁ MulOneClass.isUnital distrib).assoc }
EckmannHilton.commMonoid.description: This definition states that a type with a unital magma structure, which also distributes over a unital binary operation, qualifies as a commutative monoid.

MulHom.noncommCoprod.code:
MulHom.noncommCoprod.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {M : Type u_1} {N : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [Mul M] [Mul N] [Semigroup P]
  (f : M →ₙ* P) (g : N →ₙ* P) (comm : ∀ (m : M) (n : N), Commute (f m) (g n)) : M × N →ₙ* P
MulHom.noncommCoprod.comment:
Coproduct of two `MulHom`s with the same codomain with `Commute` assumption:
`f.noncommCoprod g _ (p : M × N) = f p.1 * g p.2`.
(For the commutative case, use `MulHom.coprod`)

explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Commute.mul_mul_mul_comm: This theorem establishes that every element is equal to itself, illustrating the reflexivity property of equality.
explanatories.MulHom.map_mul': There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

MulHom.noncommCoprod.fullDefinition: def noncommCoprod : M × N →ₙ* P where   toFun mn := f mn.fst * g mn.snd   map_mul' mn mn' := by simpa using (comm _ _).mul_mul_mul_comm _ _
MulHom.noncommCoprod.description: This definition describes a way to combine two multiplicative homomorphisms into a new homomorphism by taking their coproduct under the condition that their images commute with one another.

MonoidHom.noncommCoprod.comment:
Coproduct of two `MonoidHom`s with the same codomain,
with a commutation assumption:
`f.noncommCoprod g _ (p : M × N) = f p.1 * g p.2`.
(Noncommutative case; in the commutative case, use `MonoidHom.coprod`.)

MonoidHom.noncommCoprod.fullDefinition: def noncommCoprod : M × N →* P where   toFun := fun mn ↦ (f mn.fst) * (g mn.snd)   map_one' := by simp only [Prod.fst_one, Prod.snd_one, map_one, mul_one]   __ := f.toMulHom.noncommCoprod g.toMulHom comm
